apple-tv-military-discount: Apple does not offer a military or veteran discount on the Apple TV streaming subscription (the service formerly called Apple TV+). As of June 2026, Apple TV is $12.99/month after a 7-day free trial, the same price for everyone. Apple’s well-known 10% military discount, verified through ID.me, applies only to Apple hardware and accessories — not to the streaming service or any Apple subscription.

That doesn’t mean service members are out of options. Apple offers several standard (non-military) ways to watch Apple TV for free or for less: a 7-day free trial, 3 months free when you buy a qualifying new Apple device, free access bundled with an Apple Music Student plan, and the Apple One bundle that combines Apple TV with iCloud+, Apple Music, and more.

This is an independent guide from NavyWeek. We are not affiliated with Apple. Apple controls all pricing and terms and can change them at any time; always confirm current offers on Apple’s official pages before subscribing.
ringconn-military-discount: Does RingConn offer a military discount? The straight answer is no. RingConn does not offer a military, veteran, or first-responder discount, and it doesn’t use ID.me, GovX, or SheerID. Any "RingConn military code" you see on a coupon site is just a public sitewide code relabeled for search — anyone can use it, and the advertised percentages are frequently inflated.

The good news is that RingConn’s whole pitch already saves service members money: there’s no subscription. The Gen 3 is $349, the Gen 2 is $299, and the Gen 2 Air is $199 — and every health feature is included with no monthly fee, unlike Oura and other rings that charge a recurring membership.

For the best real price, pay with HSA/FSA funds (RingConn is HSA/FSA eligible via Flex — effectively your tax rate off the sticker), use the trade-in program for up to $70 off an old ring or wearable, and apply any working public promo code at checkout. This is an independent guide — we’re not affiliated with RingConn, and prices and codes change, so confirm the current terms at ringconn.com before you buy.
dbrand-military-discount: dbrand does not offer a military or veteran discount. There’s no dbrand military program, no ID.me or SheerID verification, and no "military code" to enter at checkout — none of dbrand’s own support, FAQ, or terms pages mention one, and dbrand famously doesn’t run identity-based discounts.

If you’ve seen a "dbrand military discount" for 10%, 20%, 35%, or 50% on a coupon site, those numbers are fabricated; they contradict each other precisely because none of them come from dbrand. Even CouponFollow’s own page concedes it "hasn’t seen a student discount or military discount offered at dbrand."

The real way to save at dbrand is the same for everyone: wait for one of dbrand’s public site-wide sales (Black Friday and other seasonal drops), take a first-order or newsletter offer if one is live, or choose lower-cost items like a skin over a case. Your military status won’t unlock anything extra. This is an independent guide; we’re not affiliated with dbrand, and dbrand can change its policies at any time.
longhorn-military-discount: LongHorn Steakhouse does not publish an official, company-wide everyday military or veteran discount — and it’s worth knowing that up front. Darden’s own discount partner, ID.me, says it isn’t aware of any LongHorn military discount, and Darden has no all-locations policy. The "10% military discount, just show your ID" you’ll see on coupon sites is location and manager discretion — a possible courtesy at some restaurants, never a guarantee. Always ask your specific LongHorn before you order.

What is real and recurring is LongHorn’s Veterans Day offer: in recent years, 10% off the meal plus a free appetizer or dessert for the table, for active-duty service members, retirees, and veterans who show proof of service (military ID, VA card, or DD214), dine-in or call-in. For everyday value anyone can count on, join the LongHorn eClub for a free appetizer on signup, and — if you buy Darden gift cards — time it to a "buy $500, get $50" bonus for roughly 9% off future meals.
This is an independent guide. We’re not affiliated with LongHorn, Darden Restaurants, or ID.me, and terms can change at any time.
hers-military-discount: Hers does not offer a blanket military discount across its telehealth categories. The one real service-member benefit is narrow: the Hims & Hers Service Appreciation Initiative, which gives U.S. military, veterans, teachers, nurses, and first responders up to 50% off compounded semaglutide GLP-1 weight-loss subscriptions — as low as $99/month.

If you are shopping Hers for hair, skin, mental-health, or sexual-health treatments, your military status will not get you a discount there; those follow standard pricing. And because compounded semaglutide is heavily affected by regulatory shifts, always confirm current terms at forhers.com/appreciation before enrolling.
This is an independent guide and not medical advice. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Hims & Hers, which controls the terms and can change them at any time.
publix-military-discount: Publix offers a 10% military discount on Veterans Day (November 11) only — for veterans, active military, and their families, on in-store grocery purchases, redeemed by showing a veteran or military ID, discharge document, or a driver’s license with a veteran designation at the register or self-checkout. It’s a genuine annual gesture Publix has run at a steady 10% for years, but it is not an everyday discount, there is no online version, and Publix does not offer a separate first-responder discount.

Here’s the honest part: for the other 364 days a year, Publix’s ordinary public savings actually beat 10%. Weekly BOGO deals (30+ every week), free Club Publix digital coupons, and coupon-stacking (one manufacturer plus one Publix or competitor coupon per item) routinely save more than a flat 10% — and pairing any grocery trip with a grocery-cashback credit card adds roughly 3–6% on top. If you have commissary access, the tax-free on-base grocery store is usually the cheapest everyday channel of all.
This is an independent guide — we’re not affiliated with Publix Super Markets — and Publix controls the terms and can change them at any time.
houston-zoo-military-discount: The Houston Zoo gives U.S. veterans and active military 50% off general admission, for up to five guests (2 adults + 3 children), all year long. It is one of the more generous zoo military discounts because it covers a whole small family, not just the service member.

Two things to know: the Zoo sells tickets online only (a reservation is required), and you will either verify your status through SheerID to get a discount code or show a valid military ID at the gate — and you must show proof of service when you check in.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with the Houston Zoo, which controls the terms and can change them at any time; flex pricing means dollar amounts vary by date.
dennis-kirk-military-discount: Does Dennis Kirk offer a military discount? No. There is no standing military percentage, no military promo code, and no ID.me, SheerID, or GovX verification path on denniskirk.com. The company supports the military community through charity and events — including “The Patriot Ride” it ran from 2006 to 2019 — but that is philanthropy, not a customer discount.

Because there is no military deal to claim, the smartest way to save is the paths open to everyone: Dennis Kirk’s Low Price Guarantee (it beats a qualifying competitor’s price by a dollar on select categories and items over $100), free shipping on orders over $89, same-day shipping, and its rotating public promotions and email sign-up offer.

This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Dennis Kirk, and Dennis Kirk controls its policies and can change them at any time. Ignore any coupon site claiming a Dennis Kirk military percentage — those codes are fabricated.
american-eagle-military-discount: Does American Eagle offer a military discount? Not officially. American Eagle Outfitters — which runs both American Eagle and Aerie — does not advertise a military or veteran discount on ae.com, and it does not offer a military discount online. ID.me, the verification service many retailers use, confirms American Eagle does not partner with it for a military discount.

The only military offer we could corroborate is a roughly 10% off in-store discount when you show a valid military ID at checkout — but this appears to be managed at the store level, not a guaranteed AE corporate policy. We found it on a shopping-center (Tanger Outlets) listing rather than on American Eagle’s own website, so participation and terms can vary by location and change at any time.

This is an independent guide, not affiliated with American Eagle Outfitters. Because AE does not publish these terms itself, call your local AE or Aerie store to confirm before you shop, and don’t expect a military discount at ae.com checkout.
frigidaire-military-discount: Yes — Frigidaire offers a military discount, verified through SheerID (not ID.me or GovX). It comes in two tiers that are easy to mix up: verified military members and first responders get 10% off home appliances, while military members, first responders, and teachers get a much bigger 25% off parts, accessories, and filters bought on Frigidaire.com. That 25% parts-and-filters tier is the real prize — it is the cheapest way to buy Frigidaire water filters and genuine OEM parts.

For a whole appliance, be honest with yourself before you burn the one-time code: the 10% often loses to a normal retailer sale. Frigidaire fridges, ranges, and washers are routinely marked down more than 10% at big-box retailers all year, and open-box or scratch-and-dent units go deeper still — so price-check the 10% code against the live public sale first.

This is an independent guide to help you use the offer. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Frigidaire, and Frigidaire controls these tiers and can change the terms or percentages at any time. Confirm the current offer on frigidaire.com/en/discounts before you buy.
hilton-military-discount: Hilton offers a Military Family Rate giving active-duty, reserve, and retired service members, veterans, and their families discounted leisure-stay pricing at participating hotels across its brands. You book it directly on Hilton.com or in the Hilton Honors app by choosing the Military Rate under "Special Rates," and you show a valid military ID at check-in.

Hilton describes this as "exclusive savings" and notes that the actual rate varies by hotel and travel dates rather than guaranteeing one fixed percentage. It applies to leisure stays only — not official government or military travel, which uses Hilton’s separate per diem rates.
This is an independent guide, not affiliated with Hilton. Hilton sets and can change the terms at any time; verify current pricing and eligibility on Hilton.com before booking.
disneyland-hotel-military-discount: Does the Disneyland Hotel have a military discount? Yes. The Disneyland Hotel is part of Disney’s 2026 Military Room Discount, which gives eligible U.S. service members and their spouses "great rates on select rooms" at all three Disneyland Resort hotels. Because hotels are rate-based, there is no published percentage — the savings vary by your dates, room type, and a limited number of military-rate rooms. You book it by phone at (866) 309-9737 (it can’t be booked online), and you show a valid military ID at check-in.

Here’s the honest way to read this: the military rate is usually the deepest on-property discount if you’re eligible and book early, but it can’t be combined with the Disney Visa rate, the AAA rate, or any public offer — you pick the single lowest for your dates. Third-party sites quote "up to 35% off the Disneyland Hotel," but that’s an estimate from Disney’s old fixed structure, not a number Disney publishes today. The only reliable figure is the one the agent quotes you for your specific nights.

This is an independent guide — NavyWeek is not affiliated with or endorsed by Disney or the Disneyland Resort. Disney controls all rates, dates, and terms and can change or end the offer at any time; always confirm on Disneyland’s official offer page and by phone before you book.
boden-military-discount: Yes — Boden offers a 20% military discount on full-price items, verified through SheerID, and the same 20% also covers medical workers, first responders, students, and teachers. The current offer runs through December 31, 2026. There’s a catch worth knowing: the 20% is barred on Sale, Clearance, Multibuy, and Gift Card items, and it can’t be combined with Boden’s public promo codes — so the smartest play depends on whether you’re buying full-price or markdown goods.

For full-price shopping, the best total-savings path is the 20% SheerID code plus a cashback portal (TopCashback was ~4.04% as of July 18, 2026), which the code doesn’t block. For sale items, skip the hero code (it’s excluded) and stack the public markdown with cashback instead.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Boden; Boden controls the terms and can change them at any time. Always confirm current details on Boden’s official page before you buy.
pandora-military-discount: Pandora jewelry gives verified members of the military community 10% off through its Supporting Heroes program. You confirm your status with ID.me, then get a promo code to use at checkout — online at pandora.net or in-store at participating Pandora retailers.

The offer is open to the broad military community that ID.me verifies: active-duty service members, National Guard and Reserve, veterans, retirees, military spouses, and immediate family members/dependents. The code is single-use, good for 60 days, and can’t be stacked with other promotions.
NavyWeek is an independent guide. We are not affiliated with Pandora. Pandora sets and can change these terms at any time; verify current details on Pandora’s official site before you buy.
jegs-military-discount: Short answer: JEGS does not publish a military or veteran discount. ID.me’s JEGS page says it plainly — "We’re not aware that JEGS offers Military discounts" — and JEGS’ own help center contains no military-discount policy anywhere; its only military-specific article covers APO/FPO shipping. The "10% JEGS military discount via ID.me" you’ll see on coupon sites does not exist at checkout.

Two honest caveats. First, hot-rodders have long reported an unofficial route: some shoppers say emailing service details to JEGS customer service got them roughly 10% account pricing that varied by brand — discretionary, never documented by JEGS, and unverified today. Second, the verified savings at JEGS are open to everyone and genuinely good: a self-serve Price Match Guarantee against Summit Racing, Sold-by-Amazon, and verified eBay stores; recurring tiered promo codes (check jegs.com/Deals for the current one); 2% Rakuten cashback; free shipping at $199+; and the Garage Sale clearance and scratch-and-dent section. Cross-shoppers should also know Summit Racing runs a real ~10% manual military discount.

teva-military-discount: Does Teva offer a military discount? Straight answer: no. Teva does not offer a military or veteran discount, ID.me itself says it is not aware of one, Teva has no first-responder program, and Teva is not sold on the GovX military marketplace. There is no code, no ID.me military rate, and no DD-214 path.

The good news is you do not need one to save. Teva’s own Sale and outlet routinely cut 20–40% off, the public email/SMS signup gives everyone about 10% on a full-price pair, ID.me Shop cashback adds a small rebate on full-price $50+ orders, and REI — which stocks Teva widely — pays Co-op members a roughly 10% annual dividend on top of member sales.

This is an independent guide — not affiliated with Teva or Deckers, and terms can change at any time. We deliberately do not cite a Teva "military percentage" because none is published. Confirm current offers at teva.com before you buy.
champs-sports-military-discount: Straight answer: Champs Sports gives 10% off most purchases to the military community, verified through SheerID online or a military ID in store. It covers active-duty service members, veterans, National Guard, Reserve members, and registered dependents of active-duty or retiree service members.

Two things keep it modest: some products are excluded (expect marquee sneaker launches and select brands to be left out), and each verification caps the discount at $100, with up to four verifications per rolling 30 days. Because the 10% can't be combined with other offers, Champs' frequent 20–40% sales usually beat it — so time your buy around a sale, and fall back to the military 10% when nothing better is live. Champs is a Foot Locker, Inc. brand, so the same 10% SheerID deal runs at Foot Locker and Kids Foot Locker.
This is an independent guide — NavyWeek is not affiliated with Champs Sports or Foot Locker, Inc., and terms change. Confirm current terms on Champs' official military discount page before you buy.
gymshark-military-discount: Gymshark gives a 10% military and veteran discount in the United States through its verification partner WeSalute (formerly Veterans Advantage). If you’re active-duty, a veteran, a retiree, current or former Guard or Reserve, or an immediate family member, you can verify your status with WeSalute and shop a private Gymshark store where 10% comes off your order at checkout.

The discount is everyday — it’s available year-round, not a limited-time promo — and Gymshark says it can be combined with public sales plus free standard shipping on orders of $75 or more. The discount applies at online checkout and can’t be added to an order after it’s placed.

This is an independent guide to help you use the offer. We’re not affiliated with Gymshark or WeSalute. Gymshark sets and can change these terms at any time, so confirm the current offer on Gymshark’s official Discounts page before you buy.
darn-tough-military-discount: Yes — Darn Tough Vermont gives verified military members 20% off at darntough.com, and it’s one of the more generous programs in the outdoor world: active duty, veterans, and retirees all qualify, and the company explicitly welcomes purchases for your spouse, kids, and household. Verification runs through VerifyPass (not ID.me — despite what coupon sites say), and the discount arrives as a code you apply at checkout.

Because Darn Tough almost never marks down its own socks, that 20% is genuinely the best everyday price for most people — and every pair carries an unconditional lifetime guarantee, so a worn-through sock gets replaced free, forever. Below we compare the 20% against GovX, ExpertVoice pro pricing, cashback portals, the military exchanges, and retailer closeouts so you can see exactly when each path wins.

This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Darn Tough Vermont, which controls these terms and can change them at any time — confirm the current program on the official Exclusive Discounts page.
mount-vernon-military-discount: Searching for the Mt. Vernon military discount? George Washington’s Mount Vernon offers military visitors a tiered set of benefits, not one flat coupon. Every day, military members (and teachers) get $4 off daytime General Admission by verifying with ID.me. But two better deals exist if you qualify: Purple Heart recipients get in free year-round, and on Veterans Day (November 11) admission is free for all active-duty, former, and retired military — the service member only; family and guests pay.
If you plan to come back, a Mount Vernon membership is $20 off for military and includes a full year of free daytime admission — the smart move for repeat visitors and locals.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Mount Vernon; the estate sets its own admission and discount terms and can change them at any time.
take-5-military-discount: Take 5 Oil Change gives military personnel a 25% discount on any oil change, year-round. Per Take 5’s own newsroom announcement and coupons page, the offer is for those who are active, reserve, or retired, and you redeem it in person by showing proof of service or a valid government-issued military ID at the shop.

There is no online checkout for oil changes, so this is an in-shop discount. Take 5’s coupons page notes coupons are valid only when emailed or texted to you (which requires opting into Take 5’s marketing messages) and that coupons typically can’t be combined with other offers — so plan to use the military discount on its own.

This is an independent guide from NavyWeek. We are not affiliated with Take 5 Oil Change or Driven Brands. Take 5 sets and can change these terms, and participation may vary by location — confirm with your local shop before you go.
trijicon-military-discount: Does Trijicon offer a military discount? Not as a flat percentage at its own checkout, and there is no "trijicon.com military code." Instead, Trijicon’s official Military / Law Enforcement / Government Programs page points qualifying shoppers to two pro-purchase programs — ExpertVoice and Guidefitter — for special MIL/LE pricing on select optics. Active-duty, reserve, National Guard, veterans, and law enforcement can verify free through either program; first responders, government, and outdoor pros also qualify through Guidefitter.

Here’s the honest part: Trijicon publishes no percentage, and on a high-demand product like the RMR the gated pro price often only ties the open street price (frequently ~$569–$599 vs the $779 MSRP) that anyone can get with no verification. The single deepest documented path is buying an eligible RMR LED model during one of Trijicon’s periodic $100 factory rebate windows (most recently April 3–May 31, 2026) — a public rebate open to everyone, not just the military. There’s also a GovX storefront for verified service members and first responders.

This independent guide maps the real routes — the two pro programs, GovX, open street pricing, and the rebate — with the exact verification mechanics, and it debunks the fake "10%–25% at trijicon.com" claim. We’re not affiliated with Trijicon, ExpertVoice, Guidefitter, or GovX, and terms can change at any time.

lg-military-discount: LG Electronics gives active-duty service members and veterans a verified discount through its LG Appreciation Program. Once you confirm your status with ID.me, you shop the LG Partner Store at LG.com, where LG guarantees a minimum of an extra 10% off LG-branded appliances and electronics — or an extra 15% off LG STUDIO and LG SIGNATURE appliances — measured against LG.com sale prices. The same eligibility path covers nurses and medical providers, first responders, teachers, students, and government employees.
There is no coupon code to enter: the savings are built into the prices you see after you sign in to the Partner Store. The program is online-only at LG.com and limited to the United States.
NavyWeek is an independent guide. We are not affiliated with LG Electronics. LG sets and can change these terms at any time; verify the current offer on LG.com before buying.
orvis-military-discount: Short answer: Orvis does have a military discount — 10% off select full-price apparel and dog gear per WeSalute’s terms — but it is only for paid WeSalute+ (Veterans Advantage) members, it works online only at orvis.com, and it excludes fishing gear, sale items, and 45+ brands. WeSalute+ costs $59.95 your first year, so the discount usually costs more than it saves. And as of July 13, 2026, WeSalute flags the Orvis benefit as "currently being updated by the partner" — it may be paused entirely. There is no ID.me, SheerID, or GovX route: ID.me says plainly that it is not aware of any Orvis military discount.

Here is the honest math: Orvis gives every new email subscriber 15% off their first order — free, no membership, no verification — which beats the military 10% outright. And the Orvis sale section (roughly 9–71% off as of July 13, 2026, including the fly gear every code excludes) beats both.

This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Orvis or WeSalute; they set and can change or pause these terms at any time — confirm the current status on the official pages before you buy.
mac-cosmetics-military-discount: Yes — MAC Cosmetics offers a 15% military discount at maccosmetics.com, and it covers veterans as well as active-duty, Guard, and Reserve members. You verify once through SheerID, get a one-time promo code, and use it at online checkout; the code is reusable once every 30 days. It’s part of MAC’s wider Appreciation Discount (medical workers get 25%; students, teachers, and first responders also get 15%).

The catch that saves you the most money: the 15% code can’t be combined with anything else. So when MAC runs one of its periodic sitewide sales of 25–30% off, that sale beats the military code — take the sale instead. Otherwise, the 15% verification is the best everyday path online.

This is an independent guide from NavyWeek. We are not affiliated with MAC Cosmetics or The Estée Lauder Companies. MAC sets the terms and can change them at any time. (Note: this is MAC Cosmetics makeup — not Apple "Mac" computers or Macy’s.)
ticketmaster-military-discount: Ticketmaster does not have a single, across-the-board military or veteran discount the way some retailers do. Instead, Ticketmaster says military discounts are "generally only available through the venue’s box office," and when an offer is available online it shows up as a ticket-type option that the specific team, venue, or artist chose to enable for that event.

The two real ways service members and veterans save through Ticketmaster are GovX and Vet Tix. GovX is a free verification membership; participating Ticketmaster event organizers use it to offer exclusive discounted tickets to military, veterans, first responders, law enforcement, government employees, and EMS. Vet Tix, run by the Veteran Tickets Foundation, gives active military and veterans free tickets to eligible events.

This is an independent guide. Discounts vary by event, are controlled by the event organizer, and many events have no military offer at all — always confirm the current offer on the official Ticketmaster event page before buying.
adobe-military-discount: Does Adobe offer a military discount? Not directly. Adobe’s own Special Offers page lists intro pricing, a big student/teacher education discount (over 71% off — $19.99/mo the first year), and business plans — but no military or veteran offer. There is no Adobe-direct military ID.me or GovX checkout button.

The only "Adobe military discount" that exists runs through a paid third-party membership, WeSalute (formerly Veterans Advantage), which advertises 15% off Creative Cloud and 20% off Premiere Pro to its members — so you would pay for WeSalute+ first, and the discount only counts as savings net of those dues.

For most eligible people, the cheaper move is Adobe’s education price if anyone in the household is a student or teacher, or Adobe’s public new-subscriber intro ($34.99/mo for 3 months) otherwise. Adobe’s seasonal Black Friday and back-to-school promos often beat the WeSalute 15% outright, with no membership needed.

You may also see coupon and "military law" blogs advertising a "30% off Acrobat military discount." We could not confirm that on Adobe.com — treat it as unverified. This independent guide (not affiliated with Adobe or WeSalute) lays out the honest math; always verify current prices on Adobe.com before you buy.
smith-and-wesson-military-discount: Smith & Wesson does not offer an everyday percentage off firearms for military shoppers. What it offers is the Military & Law Enforcement Rebate (formerly the American Guardians Rebate): up to $150 back on a prepaid card when you buy a new Smith & Wesson firearm or Gemtech suppressor, one rebate per purchase, claimed online after you buy and gated by a valid GovX ID.

Because it’s a rebate, not a checkout discount, the smart play is to buy your S&W at the lowest price you can find — transferred to your local FFL dealer — then file the $150 rebate on top. The two combine, since it’s a manufacturer rebate rather than a store coupon. Eligibility runs from active, retired, reserve, and disabled military and honorably discharged veterans (DD-214) through a long list of law enforcement and first responders.

This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Smith & Wesson or GovX. All firearm purchases go through a licensed dealer with a background check, and state laws may restrict certain models — terms and rebate windows can change at any time.
revzilla-military-discount: Yes — the RevZilla military discount is real. RevZilla runs an official military and first-responder discount for active-duty or retired U.S. military, police, fire, and EMS, verified through GovX ID right in your cart and applied automatically at checkout. What RevZilla never tells you up front is the amount: the site publishes no percentage (shoppers report about 5%, but that’s unverified), it can’t be combined with any other code, sale, or offer, and 70+ brands — including most big helmet names and all tires — are excluded.

That fine print changes the strategy. A first-time buyer’s public 10% email sign-up code likely beats it. Closeout pricing always beats it. And regular riders can earn more from the RPM membership (5% back plus 10% off dozens of brands) than from the military discount. The decision table below runs the numbers on a $500 gear cart.

This is an independent guide; NavyWeek is not affiliated with RevZilla or Comoto Holdings, and RevZilla controls the terms and can change them at any time. Always confirm the current offer on RevZilla’s official discount page before you buy.
athleta-military-discount: Athleta offers a 10% military discount for in-store purchases only — you show a valid military ID at the register, and there’s no app, code, or online account. Importantly, it’s in store only: it’s not valid on athleta.gap.com, and Athleta doesn’t run an online military verification (no ID.me or SheerID). ID.me’s own page even states it isn’t aware of an Athleta military discount, which is why you won’t find one at online checkout.

Athleta also doesn’t publish this discount on its website, so terms and participation can vary by store — confirm locally before you shop. For online savings, the public offers are usually better anyway: a 20% email-signup code, frequent sales/clearance, Rewards free shipping on $50+, and Athleta Preloved resale.

This is an independent guide — we’re not affiliated with Athleta or Gap Inc., and the company can change terms at any time. Because the discount isn’t brand-published, always confirm the current offer with the store before you rely on it.
anker-military-discount: Anker’s military discount is a GovX-verified "up to 20% off" offer — but as of March 18, 2026, Anker says the program on its U.S. store is temporarily discontinued, so the code may not be redeemable on chargers and power banks right now. Verification is through GovX, not ID.me. Anker’s sibling brands — Anker SOLIX (power stations), eufy (security), and soundcore (audio) — run their own GovX-verified military pages that appear to still be active, so eligible shoppers should route by product line.

Here’s the money-saving truth: Anker discounts so deeply and so often — and Amazon’s coupon-clip prices tie or beat anker.com so regularly — that the public sale usually beats the 20% military discount anyway, and the two can’t be combined.
This is an independent guide; NavyWeek is not affiliated with Anker, and Anker controls and can change these terms at any time.
pods-military-veteran: PODS offers a military discount of up to 10% off your move when you book with promo code SERV10. navy-federal-military-discount: Navy Federal doesn’t have a military discount — it has a military gate. staples-military-discount: Staples does not offer an everyday military or veteran discount — there’s no ID.me or SheerID verification at checkout, and no military promo code exists despite what coupon sites claim. tsa-precheck-military-discount: Is there a TSA PreCheck veteran discount? For most veterans, no — but that’s the least interesting part of the answer. If you’re currently serving (active duty, Guard, Reserve, Coast Guard, academy cadets, USPHS or NOAA commissioned corps) or a DoD civilian, you already have PreCheck free: your DoD ID number is your Known Traveler Number. No enrollment, no fee.

Once you leave the service that benefit ends — TSA says so explicitly — and the standard 5-year enrollment fee applies ($76.75–$85 depending on provider as of July 14, 2026). Two groups are exempt: veterans with qualifying service-connected disabilities (permanent blindness, or a VA-issued wheelchair or prosthetic limb) enroll free under the 2025 VETS Safe Travel Act, and military survivor families enroll free with a TAPS verification letter. Military spouses get $25 off. Everyone else’s best move is a credit card that reimburses the fee — TSA keeps the list.

This is an independent guide, not affiliated with TSA, DHS, or the VA. TSA PreCheck is a federal program: eligibility and fees are set by the government and can change, so always confirm current terms on tsa.gov before you enroll.
advance-auto-parts-military-discount: Advance Auto Parts offers a 10% military discount on regularly-priced items, and it’s confirmed on Advance’s own help desk, so this one’s solid. american-express-military-discount: American Express does not offer a traditional "military discount" — there is no percent-off and no promo code. What it offers is arguably more valuable: under two federal laws, eligible active-duty servicemembers (and their spouses) pay $0 in annual fees on personal Amex cards, and get interest on older balances capped at 6%.

Which benefit you get depends on one thing — when you opened the card. Open it while you are an active-duty covered borrower and the Military Lending Act (MLA) zeroes your annual fee automatically. Held the card before you went on active duty? The Servicemembers Civil Relief Act (SCRA) caps your rate at 6% and waives fees — but you have to request it.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with American Express; Amex sets and can change these terms, and eligibility is defined by federal law and Department of Defense records.
altra-military-discount: Altra Running doesn’t put an ID.me or SheerID “military discount” on altrarunning.com — instead, its official military route is ExpertVoice. If you verify as active military, a veteran, or a military spouse through ExpertVoice, your discount is applied automatically at checkout (no promo code), and Altra’s ExpertVoice group is listed at up to 40% off MSRP. There is also a GovX “Altra” marketplace (plus an “Altra Open Box” store) as a second route.

One honest catch: the ExpertVoice discount can’t be combined with anything, and if a public Altra sale is cheaper, the site charges you the sale price instead. So during deep clearance events, the public price can beat the verified discount. Everyone can also grab a 10% welcome code by joining the email list.
This is an independent guide — we’re not affiliated with Altra, ExpertVoice, or GovX, and terms can change at any time. Always confirm the current offer at the source before you buy.
rsvlts-military-discount: Does RSVLTS offer a military discount? Yes. RSVLTS runs an official, year-round 25% off sitewide discount for active-duty and veteran members of the U.S. Armed Forces. You verify your status through RSVLTS’s ID system (VerifyPass) and receive a unique code to use at checkout — available 365 days a year, straight from RSVLTS’s own military discount page.

Here’s the honest part most coupon pages leave out: 25% is also the rate RSVLTS gives new email subscribers. So if this is your first order, the newsletter welcome code can reach the same price without verifying. The military discount’s real edge is that it keeps working — a fresh 25% code for every future purchase, all year — while the welcome code is a one-time deal.
This is an independent guide. We are not affiliated with RSVLTS; we link to RSVLTS’s official pages so you can confirm the current terms before you buy.
origin-military-discount: Origin (originusa.com), the Maine-made apparel, BJJ, and boots brand, offers its military and veteran discount through GovX. Verify your status with GovX and the discount applies to regular-priced items; the exact percentage is shown only after you verify.

There is no ID.me path and no live on-site "veteran code" — the old VETERAN2020-style codes are historical. For sale items, Origin’s public 20% Off collection and seasonal sales are usually the better lever, since the GovX discount applies to full-price items only.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Origin, which controls the terms and can change them at any time; GovX sets the live discount rate.
verizon-fios-military-discount: Verizon Fios home internet has its own military discount — and it is separate from Verizon’s better-known mobile military discount. Eligible active-duty members, retirees, veterans, current or former Guard/Reserve, and Gold Star family members can register through ID.me and get a monthly discount on an eligible Fios plan (300 Mbps, 500 Mbps, 1 Gig, or 2 Gig), plus the $99 professional setup fee waived when you order online.

One thing to know up front: your Verizon mobile military discount does not automatically apply to your Fios bill — they are two different programs, each with its own ID.me registration. And on Verizon’s own military page, the Fios "military" prices currently match the standard Auto Pay + Mobile + Home bundle prices, so Verizon does not publish a separate military-only dollar figure. The concrete, military-specific wins are the waived $99 setup fee and a $5/mo discount on Fios Digital Voice or Home Device Advisor. The biggest recurring savings come from bundling a Verizon mobile line (Mobile + Home Discount).
This is an independent guide — we are not affiliated with Verizon, and prices and terms change. Confirm the exact price you see after ID.me verification before you order.
sling-tv-military-discount: Does Sling TV offer a military discount? No. As of July 14, 2026, Sling TV does not offer a military or veteran discount — not through ID.me, SheerID, GovX, or WeSalute, and not by asking support. ID.me’s own Sling TV page confirms it, stating it is not aware of any SLING TV military discount, and Sling’s deals hub lists only public promos. Any site advertising a "Sling military code" is dressing up a public offer.

The good news: Sling is already one of the cheapest live-TV services, and its public offers do the work a discount would. New subscribers typically get 50% off the first month, prepay bundles start around $49.99 for 3 months on the entry tier, and cashback portals pay a one-time bounty of up to about $15 on new signups (as of July 14, 2026). There’s also Sling Freestream, a completely free ad-supported tier.

If you specifically want a live-TV service that rewards your military status, YouTube TV runs a genuine ID.me-verified military offer ($67.99/mo for 12 months per its published terms) — Sling simply doesn’t compete on that axis. This is an independent guide; NavyWeek is not affiliated with Sling TV, DISH Network, or EchoStar, and offers can change at any time.
grand-hyatt-deer-valley-military-discoun: Grand Hyatt Deer Valley runs a genuine, property-specific military program called "Salute to Service." Eligible service members book discounted lodging through a dedicated Salute to Service portal and get spa and food-and-beverage discounts (alcohol excluded). The standout perk: if you’re staying at the property, you can buy Deer Valley lift tickets at up to 75% off the window rate — much deeper than Deer Valley Resort’s own ~25% military ticket rate.

Eligibility for the portal is broad: active duty, reserve or National Guard, retired military, 100% disabled veterans, and actively serving Department of Defense civilians. And because this is a Hyatt hotel, you can also book the chain-wide Veteran & Military Rate (code MILVET, 10–15% off the standard rate) here — a refundable rate that still earns World of Hyatt points. Since these rates don’t combine, compare the Salute to Service portal rate against MILVET and book the lower.

This is an independent guide — NavyWeek is not affiliated with Grand Hyatt, Hyatt, or Deer Valley Resort, and terms can change at any time. We break down who qualifies, how the portal works, and how the hotel program differs from the resort’s own discount, with links straight to the official sources so you can confirm current terms before booking.
outer-banks-hotels-military-discount: Is there an Outer Banks hotel military discount? Yes — but "the Outer Banks" isn’t one hotel, so there isn’t one discount. Where you save depends on what you book: a chain hotel room, a beach-house rental, or a condo week through the military’s own vacation club.

At the branded hotels (Hilton Garden Inn Outer Banks/Kitty Hawk, Hampton, Holiday Inn Express, Comfort and others), you use the parent chain’s military or "government & military" rate — a variable discount off the going rate, not a fixed percentage. Book direct, then price-check it against the chain’s advance-purchase, AAA, and senior rates, because those often come out lower — and either way sign in so your loyalty points still count. If you’re traveling on official orders, ask for the government per-diem rate instead (Dare County caps are on this page).

If you’re renting a beach house — the classic Outer Banks trip — several local property managers give active and retired military up to about 5% off full-week stays with a military ID (eligibility and amount vary by company and by home). And if you qualify, the Armed Forces Vacation Club sells 7-night condo weeks at the Outer Banks Beach Club in Kill Devil Hills from around $369–$569, which is the cheapest week of lodging on the beach. This is an independent guide; NavyWeek is not affiliated with any Outer Banks hotel, rental company, or chain, and every business here sets and can change its own terms.
vans-military-discount: If you’re searching for a Vans military or veteran discount, here’s the honest, up-to-date answer: as of June 23, 2026, Vans does not advertise a military or veteran discount on its official site (vans.com). Vans’ Current Offers page lists a Vans Family welcome deal, an SMS sign-up offer, free shipping, and seasonal sales — but no standing military discount and no military verification flow through SheerID or ID.me.

You may still see "Vans 10% military discount" on coupon and verification-aggregator sites. We checked Vans’ own pages and could not confirm any of those claims; the dedicated Vans military-discount program page now returns a 404 error. Some individual Vans retail stores have advertised in-store military discounts in the past, but that varies by location and is not a published, company-wide offer.

This is an independent guide. We’re not affiliated with Vans, and Vans controls its offers and can add or remove them at any time. Below, we cover what’s actually confirmed today and the official ways military shoppers can still save at Vans.
nfl-shop-military-discount: Yes — NFLShop.com offers a 15% military and first-responder discount, verified through ID.me at checkout. The NFL Shop military discount covers active duty, National Guard, reserves, veterans, retirees, and their spouses and dependents, plus police officers, sheriffs, and state troopers on the first-responder side. The catch is in the fine print: it’s online-only, it can’t be combined with any other promo code, and it can’t buy gift cards.

That last part matters more than the number. NFL Shop’s Outlet runs up to ~60% off, and because you can’t stack the 15% on a sale price, the public markdown usually beats the military discount outright on anything that isn’t full price. Verify for 15% on new full-price jerseys; shop Outlet for everything else.

This is an independent guide — we’re not affiliated with NFL Shop, the NFL, Fanatics, or ID.me. NFL Shop controls the discount terms and can change them at any time, so always confirm the current offer on its official Military & First Responder FAQ before you buy.
jared-military-discount: Yes — the Jared military discount is real: verified members of the military community get 10% off, verified through ID.me. Active duty, veterans, retirees, spouses, and dependents all qualify per Jared’s own eligibility FAQ, and the ID.me-issued code works both at jared.com checkout and in Jared stores.

Before you count on it, read the fine print. The 10% cannot be combined with any other offer, and a long exclusions list keeps it off clearance, custom pieces, trade-in purchases, and most designer watch brands (Tacori, TAG Heuer, Movado, Breitling, and more). Jared also runs public coupons and sales almost year-round — when one of those covers your item at 10% or better, take the public deal instead.

This is an independent guide; NavyWeek is not affiliated with Jared or Signet Jewelers, and Jared controls and can change these terms at any time. Always confirm the current offer on Jared’s official military discount page before you buy.
sixt-military-discount: SIXT rent a car gives active U.S. military members and veterans up to 15% off the daily base rate on its rental fleet. The discount covers people serving now and those who have served, across all branches of the U.S. Armed Forces plus the National Guard Reserve.

To get it, you verify your military or veteran status through GoCertify — SIXT’s verification partner — and then book through the GoCertify-linked SIXT page. No coupon code is required; SIXT applies the discounted rate automatically when you reserve through that flow. Because this is a car rental, there is no in-store coupon to hand over — everything happens online when you book.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with SIXT. SIXT sets and can change the terms at any time, so confirm the current offer on SIXT’s official page before you book.
black-rifle-coffee-military-discount: Black Rifle Coffee Company is veteran-founded, and it backs that up with a real military discount — but read the fine print. The headline offer runs through ID.me and is a new-subscription discount (currently shown as about 50% off your first Coffee Club order) for military, veterans, first responders, nurses, teachers, and government employees. Separately, BRCC runs a GovX storefront at roughly 20% off for military and first responders. There is no flat everyday percentage on a single one-time bag.

Which one saves you the most depends on what you are buying: if you are starting a subscription, the ID.me first-order discount is the clear winner; if you are grabbing a one-time order or gear, the GovX ~20% (or a live public promo code) is the move.

This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Black Rifle Coffee, and BRCC can change these terms — including the discount percentage — at any time. Confirm the live number at checkout.
aldo-military-discount: Yes — ALDO gives a 20% military discount on new-arrival (full-price) merchandise, verified through SheerID (and also available via ID.me Shop), valid both online and in store. Online, you verify once and get a single-use code to enter at checkout; in store, you show a valid military or veteran ID.

The one thing to know: it applies to full-price new arrivals only and can’t be combined with sales, loyalty rewards, or other offers — so on a style that’s already marked down, ALDO’s public sale (often 40–60% off) is usually the better price.

This is an independent guide. We’re not affiliated with ALDO, and ALDO controls the percentage, provider, and exclusions and can change them at any time. Always confirm current terms on ALDO’s military-discount page before you buy.
rei-military-discount: Does REI offer a military discount? No. REI does not offer a military or veteran discount — there is no percentage off for active-duty members, veterans, retirees, Guard/Reserve, spouses, or dependents, and REI does not use ID.me, GovX, SheerID, or WeSalute for service-member verification. ID.me itself confirms it is "not aware that REI offers Military discounts," and REI’s own help center says the same.

That doesn’t mean there’s no way to save. REI is a co-op, and its savings come from a $30 one-time, lifetime membership that anyone can buy. Members earn an annual Co-op Member Reward — REI says ~10% back on eligible full-price purchases is typical but not guaranteed — plus member-only coupons, member sale pricing, free U.S. standard shipping, and access to Re/Supply used gear. For most service members and veterans who shop at REI, the membership plus the annual reward is the real "discount."

This is an independent guide. We’re not affiliated with REI, and REI controls its membership terms and can change them at any time. Always confirm current details on REI’s official pages before you buy.
ynab-military-discount: YNAB (You Need A Budget) does not offer a military, veteran, or active-duty discount. There is no YNAB military discount program, no ID.me or SheerID verification, and no military rate at checkout — YNAB’s pricing page and its official "ways to get YNAB for free" list cover every discount the company runs, and none is for military members. Service members pay the same $109/year (or $14.99/month) as everyone else.

The good news: the best legitimate savings path is genuinely strong, and it’s open to everyone. Start the 34-day free trial (no credit card on direct signup), then lock in the $109 annual plan — about $9 a month instead of $14.99. And if you, your spouse, or a dependent is a currently enrolled college student, YNAB’s College Program gives a full year free, which beats any percentage-off military deal you’ll find anywhere.

One more honest note: coupon sites advertise YNAB "military" codes and 50%-off deals. None of them is verified on any YNAB source. This is an independent guide — NavyWeek is not affiliated with YNAB, and YNAB sets its own prices and can change them at any time.
schlitterbahn-military-discount: Straight answer: yes, Schlitterbahn has a military discount — but the two Texas parks run different programs now. At Schlitterbahn New Braunfels (operated by Six Flags), active-duty and retired military members, veterans, and first responders buy discounted tickets starting around $35 online, verified through ID.me, and can cover up to 6 friends and family — plus free parking. At Schlitterbahn Galveston (operated separately by Enchanted Parks), you get 10% off the online ticket price at the gate by showing a military ID, DD-214, veteran-designated license, or work badge at the booth.
Neither discount combines with public sales, so it’s worth comparing the military rate against whatever advance-purchase promo is live and buying the cheaper one.

This is an independent guide — we’re not affiliated with Schlitterbahn, Six Flags, or Enchanted Parks, and prices and programs can change at any time. Confirm current terms on each park’s official page before you go.
chase-military-discount: Chase doesn’t offer a “military discount” — no promo code, no percent-off. What it offers is worth far more: under the Military Lending Act, active-duty servicemembers and their spouses who open a personal Chase credit card reportedly pay $0 in annual fees — even on the $795 Sapphire Reserve — automatically, confirmed by a letter Chase mails after approval. And under the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act, Chase is consistently reported to go beyond the law’s 6% cap: 4% APR on eligible pre-service balances plus waived fees, through active duty and up to a year after.

One honest caveat: Chase publishes the process — its SCRA page and the Chase Military Services line, 1-877-469-0110 — but not the numbers. The $0-fee and 4% figures come from Chase’s mailed benefit letters and independent military-finance reporting, and this guide labels them that way. Which track you’re on comes down to one thing: when you opened the account. During covered service → MLA, automatic. Before active duty → SCRA, by request.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with JPMorgan Chase; Chase sets its terms and can change them, and eligibility is defined by federal law and Department of Defense records.
dodge-military-discount: Straight answer: Dodge gives eligible military shoppers a $500 Military Bonus Cash Allowance on select 2026 vehicles — currently the Durango (including SRT), Charger Daytona BEV, and Charger ICE. You verify through SheerID, get an authorization number, and present it at a franchised Dodge dealer.

The best part is that the $500 stacks on top of the month’s public incentives — retail bonus cash, special financing, and lease programs — so the real savings come from combining it with a strong incentive month and hard negotiation, not the $500 by itself.

The catch is veteran eligibility: honorably discharged veterans qualify only within 12 months of discharge (100% disabled veterans qualify anytime). This is an independent guide — we’re not affiliated with Dodge or Stellantis, and the eligible-model list and terms change frequently; confirm current details at dodge.com/incentives before you buy.
titanic-museum-military-discount: The Titanic Museum Attraction — the two ship-shaped museums in Pigeon Forge, TN and Branson, MO — honors military and veterans, but the best savings aren’t an everyday percentage: they’re the museum’s free-admission recognition programs in August and during Veterans Week in November. Outside those windows, service members and veterans can get a modest discount at the box office with valid ID, and Pigeon Forge offers a GOVX online path.

The two dominant deals are "Celebrate Freedom" in August (military personnel and first responders free with ID, historically at Pigeon Forge) and "Titanic Honors Veterans" during Veterans Week in November (past and present military free with a Military ID — one comp per ID, with the rest of the party getting the regular military discount). Off-program, the everyday box-office discount is small: Explore Branson’s tourism office lists about $2–$3 off, and Pigeon Forge’s exact amount should be confirmed on site.

This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with the Titanic Museum Attraction, GOVX, or any brand mentioned. Discount terms, prices, and program dates change frequently and vary by location — always confirm current details at the box office or on the official site before you buy.

It is open to active-duty US Military Service Members, Veterans, National Guard and Reserve members, and their immediate family members, as well as Police, Firefighters, and EMTs. The most important rule to know: HexClad allows only one discount per order, so the Heroes discount cannot be combined with other promotions, and it is not valid during HexClad’s sitewide sales or Black Friday / Cyber Monday events.

This is an independent guide maintained by NavyWeek. We are not affiliated with HexClad. HexClad sets and can change these terms at any time — always confirm details on HexClad’s official Heroes page before purchasing.
johnston-and-murphy-military-discount: Straight answer: Johnston & Murphy does not offer a military or veteran discount on its own website. There’s no ID.me or SheerID military gate at checkout, and ID.me itself says it’s unaware of any Johnston & Murphy military discount. Coupon sites advertising a "Johnston & Murphy military discount" with big percentages are using invented numbers.

What does work: verified service members and veterans can shop Johnston & Murphy through the GovX marketplace (and the VA-Canteen shopvcs.va.gov storefront) at member pricing — a separate storefront, not a code on the brand site. And for everyone, Johnston & Murphy runs frequent 25–30% sitewide promos plus a deep Sale/clearance section that usually beat a typical 10% military rate anyway.

This is an independent guide — NavyWeek is not affiliated with Johnston & Murphy, and the brand can change its programs at any time. Confirm current pricing at johnstonmurphy.com or govx.com before buying.
zappos-military-discount: Zappos does not currently advertise a military or veteran discount that we can confirm on Zappos.com. Zappos once ran a SheerID-verified "Programs" discount (10% off online for military, students, and teachers), but that program has been discontinued and is no longer documented on Zappos’ own help pages as of June 2026.

That doesn’t mean service members can’t save at Zappos — it just means the savings are the same ones open to every shopper: the free Zappos VIP rewards program, a one-time 10%-off code for new email subscribers, clearance and seasonal sales, and occasional sitewide promo codes. Zappos also offers free shipping and a free 365-day return window on every order.

This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Zappos. Zappos controls its own offers and can add, change, or remove a discount at any time, so always confirm current terms on Zappos.com before you buy.
finish-line-military-discount: Finish Line gives a 10% discount on in-store purchases to people who serve or have served in the U.S. military — active duty, veterans, retirees, and members of the Reserve and National Guard — along with their spouses, domestic partners, and dependents. There is no online version of this discount and no sign-up: you simply show a valid military ID (or another accepted proof of service) to the cashier when you check out at a Finish Line store.

Unlike many retailers, Finish Line does not route its military discount through ID.me, SheerID, GovX, or any other online verification service. Anyone telling you to “verify with ID.me for 20% off at Finish Line online” is mistaken — ID.me’s own website confirms Finish Line does not use it for military verification, and the official Finish Line offer is in-store only at 10%.

This is an independent guide published by NavyWeek. We are not affiliated with Finish Line, and Finish Line sets and can change these terms at any time, so confirm details with a store associate before you buy.
penfed-military-discount: PenFed — Pentagon Federal Credit Union — doesn’t have a "military discount," and despite the name it isn’t military-only: anyone in the U.S. has been able to join since its January 1, 2019 merger with Progressive Credit Union created an open charter. What PenFed does have is Honors Advantage, a membership program that gives the military community better card terms automatically: the $95 annual fee waived on its Pathfinder Rewards travel card, 4X points on travel and 3X on dining instead of 3X/2X, and a flat 2% cash back on the Power Cash card instead of 1.5%.

Here’s what makes PenFed different from the statutory fee waivers at Amex or Chase: those depend on federal law (SCRA/MLA) and end when active duty ends. Honors Advantage covers active duty, Guard, Reserve, honorably discharged veterans, and military retirees — for life — because it’s a program PenFed created, not a legal obligation. Military spouses aren’t listed in the military route, but they (like any civilian) can get identical terms by holding a qualifying PenFed checking account.

This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with PenFed, which controls Honors Advantage and all card terms and can change them at any time; PenFed is federally insured by the NCUA, and nothing here is financial advice or a credit offer.
venture-x-military: Here’s the answer most pages won’t lead with: the Venture X is not free for military members who open it while serving. Capital One does not waive annual fees under the Military Lending Act — a $395/year fee that American Express and Chase would zero out on their premium cards stays fully in place on a Venture X opened during active duty. If you arrived expecting an Amex-Platinum-style deal, it isn’t here.

What Capital One does honor — generously — is the SCRA. If your Venture X (or any Capital One or Discover account) was opened before your active-duty start date, one request gets you a 4% interest cap (better than the law’s 6%) and no fees except bona-fide insurance — the $395 fee effectively goes to $0, retroactive to your first day of active duty, until a year after you leave. Guard and Reserve members can even set this up deliberately: a card opened between activations qualifies at the next set of 30+ day orders.

And if you can’t get the waiver but still want the card, do the math with clear eyes: the $300 Capital One Travel credit plus 10,000 anniversary miles roughly cancel the fee — but only if you’d actually book through Capital One Travel. This is an independent guide; NavyWeek is not affiliated with Capital One, which sets these terms and can change them.
petco-military-discount: Petco does not offer a military or veteran discount in 2026 — there’s no program on petco.com, no in-store policy, and ID.me itself says it’s "not aware of Petco offering Military community discounts." The 10% you may remember was real, but it belonged to Petco’s on-base Exchange store at Joint Base Lewis-McChord (announced 2019), and store employees confirm there’s no active chain-wide discount today — just leftover signage and the occasional manager’s-discretion markdown near bases.

Here’s what actually works: GovX members can buy Petco digital gift cards at 10% off and spend them online or in-store on anything, including sale items — the closest thing to a standing military discount Petco has. And Petco’s public 35% off your first Repeat Delivery order beats any military discount claim you’ll find on coupon sites.
This is an independent guide — we’re not affiliated with Petco, GovX, or ID.me. Terms change; confirm before you buy.
camelbak-military-discount: CamelBak’s military savings run through two verified routes — not a simple "20% off on camelbak.com" that coupon sites claim. First, the GovX marketplace operates a CamelBak brand store with member pricing for verified military, veterans, first responders, and government (great for hard-to-find mil-spec hydration like Crux and Antidote reservoirs). Second, CamelBak runs a Pro Purchase program through ExpertVoice for verified pros — which for gear brands usually means deeper discounts than any public military percentage, with personal-use and no-resale terms.

If you qualify on ExpertVoice, that’s typically the deepest deal. If not, compare the GovX store, the tax-free military exchange (CamelBak is stocked at AAFES/NEX), and current retail sales. The widely-repeated "flat 20% via ID.me on camelbak.com" couldn’t be confirmed on a CamelBak source, so we don’t promise it.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with CamelBak, GovX, or ExpertVoice, and all three control their terms and can change them at any time.
uag-military-discount: Yes — the UAG military discount is real: a first-party 20% off select urbanarmorgear.com orders. You verify through VerifyPass (not ID.me) and get a single-use code for 20% off at checkout. Eligible groups are military, veterans, first responders, and teachers, with government employees and healthcare workers also served through the VerifyPass portal.

The catch worth knowing: the 20% applies to full-price items only, can’t be combined with other codes or clearance, and UAG allows one code per order. Because UAG runs frequent 20–30% public sales and a permanent clearance section, the best deal on any given day is often the public price — not your discount. Verify for the 20% on full-price new releases; buy the public price when a 25%+ sale or clearance markdown is live.
This is an independent guide. We’re not affiliated with UAG; UAG sets the terms and can change them at any time — confirm the current offer on the official Service Rewards page before you buy.
msc-military-discount: Yes — MSC Cruises offers a real military discount: 5% off Interior and Ocean View staterooms and 10% off Balcony, Suite, and MSC Yacht Club (Deluxe Suite) staterooms, for active and retired US and Canadian military and Department of Defense personnel, with immediate family (spouses, parents, in-laws, dependent children) included when the service member or employee sails with them. You get it by asking for the "Military Discount" promotion when booking — call MSC at 877-665-4655 or use a travel agent — and by showing an ID badge from your organization at the time of booking. The discount can cover multiple staterooms, and MSC adds real redeployment protection: cancel at least 15 days out with a commanding officer’s letter and receive 100% future cruise credit good for two years.

Two things to know before you call. First, MSC’s published terms cover active and retired personnel — veterans who separated without retiring aren’t listed, so don’t count on it without asking. Second, the discount is capacity controlled and cannot be combined with any other discount or promotion, including the Voyagers Club 5% — so when MSC is running one of its frequent public sales (up to 30% off plus onboard credit at the time of this review), price your sailing both ways and book the cheaper fare.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with MSC Cruises; MSC sets and can change these terms at any time.
allstate-military-discount: Does Allstate offer a military discount? Short answer: not nationwide. Allstate’s published auto-insurance discounts are bundling, safe-driving (Drivewise), responsible-payer, anti-theft, anti-lock-brake, and good-student — none of them military-specific (allstate.com, verified July 11, 2026). There is no Allstate national military, veteran, or deployment discount and no online military-verification code.

The one exception is Louisiana, where state law (R.S. 22:1482) forces every insurer — Allstate included — to give qualifying military drivers a 25% premium discount. That is a state mandate, not an Allstate perk, and it does not exist outside Louisiana. six-flags-military-discount: Six Flags offers discounted single-day admission for U.S. military members (active and retired), veterans, first responders, and their immediate family members.
