There’s no active-duty, veteran, retiree, Guard/Reserve, or military-spouse discount on annieselke.com, and the brand isn’t on ID.me, GovX, or WeSalute and runs no SheerID military offer. The only credential-based program Annie Selke has is its Trade Program for interior designers, architects, and resellers — a business account, not a military benefit.

You may see coupon sites advertising a “20% Annie Selke military discount” or a code like “OPENAIR.” That’s a general public promo code, not a service-gated military offer, and the SheerID “military save 15%” page those sites point to actually belongs to a different retailer. We’d rather tell you the military discount doesn’t exist than send you chasing a code that isn’t what it claims to be.

The good news: Annie Selke runs genuinely deep public sales — routinely up to 70% off rugs and bedding in the Sale and Last Chance sections — plus free shipping on all contiguous-US orders. For most shoppers that beats any percentage-off code. This is an independent guide; we’re not affiliated with Annie Selke, and the brand can change its terms at any time.
red-robin-military-discount: Red Robin does not offer an everyday, year-round percentage discount for military or veterans — so ignore any "flat 10–20% off for vets" you see on coupon sites. What Red Robin does run is a genuine, long-standing Veterans Day promotion: a free Red’s Big Tavern Burger with a bottomless side, dine-in, for veterans and active-duty service members who show proof of service on November 11.

The rest of the year, your real savings come from the free Red Robin Royalty program — you earn a point per dollar (100 points = a $10 reward), get a free appetizer when you join, and a birthday treat — plus whatever public app or email deals are live. Military-editorial sites also report a 15% Royalty-member discount during July, but that is not published on Red Robin’s own site, so confirm it at your location before counting on it.

This is an independent guide — we’re not affiliated with Red Robin Gourmet Burgers, Inc. Most Red Robins are franchised, every offer is "at participating locations," and Red Robin can change or end any program at any time.
ihop-military-discount: IHOP does not publish a corporate everyday military or veteran discount. Because nearly all IHOP restaurants are independently owned and operated, any year-round discount for service members is set by the individual location, not by IHOP corporate — so it varies and is not guaranteed. Your best bet is to call your local IHOP and ask before you go.

What IHOP does promote nationally is its annual Veterans Day offer: on November 11, veterans and active-duty military can get free Red, White & Blueberry Pancakes (or a pancake combo at select locations), dine-in only, at participating U.S. restaurants, with proof of service.
This is an independent guide from NavyWeek. We are not affiliated with IHOP. IHOP controls its offers and can change or end them at any time; confirm current terms with IHOP or your local restaurant.
kia-military-discount: Kia offers eligible service members, retirees, and their spouses a Military Bonus — a flat cash incentive, currently $500 (some program periods run $400) — applied at a Kia dealer toward the purchase or lease of a new Kia. It is officially the Kia America Military Specialty Incentive Program. It is not a percentage off, and there is no online military code: you prove your status with paper documents at the dealership, and a plain military ID by itself is not accepted.

The smart move isn’t the $500 by itself — it’s stacking the Military Bonus on top of whatever national APR or Cash Back offer Kia is running on your model that month, then negotiating the vehicle price separately. Kia explicitly allows the bonus to combine with its Special APR and Cash Back programs when you qualify.

This is an independent guide from NavyWeek. We are not affiliated with Kia; the program amount and eligible-vehicle list change every program period, and Kia can change or end the offer at any time — always confirm the current terms with your local Kia dealer before you sign.
road-runner-sports-military-discount: Road Runner Sports offers a reported ~10% military and first-responder discount, verified through ID.me — but two things matter more than the number. First, it applies to full-price items only and can’t be combined with sales, clearance, or other promo codes. Second, it usually isn’t the best deal on the site.

Road Runner Sports builds its savings around a paid loyalty membership, VIP Family Rewards: 10% instant savings every day on shoes, apparel, and gear — and unlike the military discount, VIP’s 10% works during sales and earns Rewards Cash you can spend later. VIP costs $1.99 for the first 6 months, then $49.99 a year (cancelable, with a prorated refund). So for anyone who buys running gear more than occasionally, VIP beats the non-combinable military 10% — and when a big public sale is live (often 30–60% off), the public price beats both.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Road Runner Sports, and terms can change at any time.
helly-hansen-military-discount: Helly Hansen offers US and Canada military members 20% off online through SheerID verification — the clean, verifiable everyday deal. Helly Hansen also runs a separate, application-based military membership whose discount is discretionary and not published (it "varies between individuals," shown only in your account), so it may or may not beat 20%.

Some directory and coupon sites claim "35% off" for Helly Hansen military, but Helly Hansen’s own pages do not confirm that figure. Because Helly Hansen runs deep seasonal sales that the 20% code cannot combine with, a big public markdown sometimes beats the discount outright.

This is an independent guide; we are not affiliated with Helly Hansen. Helly Hansen controls these terms and can change them at any time, so confirm current details on its official military page before you buy.
amex-gold-military: Is the Amex Gold free for military? Yes — for active-duty servicemembers and their spouses, the card’s $325 annual fee drops to $0, and not through a promo code. Under the Military Lending Act (MLA), American Express adjusts the annual fee to $0 on personal cards opened while you’re a covered borrower. It’s automatic: Amex checks Department of Defense records at application, and the $0 fee applies the moment the account opens. The card’s up-to-$424-a-year credit lineup and its 4x points at restaurants and U.S. supermarkets keep working exactly as they do for anyone else — which makes the Gold, for a covered borrower, better than free.

Already had the Gold before going on active duty? Then the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act (SCRA) is your route — it caps interest at 6%, and because Amex counts annual membership fees as "interest" under SCRA, the fee is waived for your active-duty period. Unlike MLA, you must request it. And the honest fine print most pages skip: veterans and retirees no longer on active duty get no ongoing waiver.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with American Express; Amex sets card terms and fee amounts, and eligibility is defined by federal law and Department of Defense records.
factor-military-discount: Factor (Factor_, formerly Factor75) runs a Hero Discount Program for verified military members, veterans, and first responders — plus medical providers, nurses, hospital employees, and teachers. You get 55% off your first box with free shipping, then 15% off every box for the next year (about 51 boxes). Verify through ID.me or GovX and the savings apply automatically at checkout.

The discount can’t be combined with other promotions or gift cards, and it’s for new customers (or accounts closed more than a day earlier). The whole offer runs for 380 days, so it’s best if you plan to keep the subscription past the first box.

This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Factor or HelloFresh. Factor controls the terms and can change them at any time; confirm current details on Factor’s Hero Discounts page before you order.
southwest-military-discount: Does Southwest offer a military discount? Yes — but as unpublished "Military fares" plus active-duty perks, not a flat percentage off airfare. Southwest offers special Military fares for active-duty U.S. service members and their authorized dependents, and two notable active-duty travel benefits: a checked-baggage fee exemption and priority boarding. Southwest does not publish a discount percentage, and Military fares cannot be booked online — you book them by phone or at a ticket counter and show a valid Uniformed Services ID at check-in.

Important for veterans and retirees: Southwest’s official Military-fare eligibility list covers active-duty members (including reservists and National Guard on orders, Coast Guard on active orders, and service-academy cadets) and their authorized dependents. Veterans and retirees are not named as eligible for the Military fare, though they can book any of Southwest’s standard fares like any traveler.

This is an independent guide, not affiliated with Southwest Airlines. Southwest controls all terms and can change them at any time; always confirm current details on Southwest’s official Military Travel page before you book.
delta-military-discount: Does Delta offer a military discount? Mostly as policy perks for active-duty service members — not a flat percentage off airfare. If you are active duty in the Army, Marine Corps, Navy, Air Force, Space Force, or Coast Guard, Delta gives you free checked-bag exceptions (more free bags than civilian passengers, whether you are on orders or traveling for leisure), early boarding, special military pet-travel rules, and savings on Delta Vacations® packages.

Delta also references “a military discount on flights,” but it does not publish a percentage online. Military and leisure military fares are unpublished — you book them by messaging Delta or calling, not with an online promo code. You show your military ID (and your orders, when traveling on orders) at the ticket counter to claim the bag and boarding benefits.

This is an independent guide to help you use these benefits. We are not affiliated with Delta Air Lines, and Delta controls the terms and can change them at any time. Always confirm the current details on Delta’s official military-travel page before you book.
lifelock-military-discount: LifeLock — now Norton 360 with LifeLock — does not publish a standalone everyday military discount on its consumer site. The legitimate military channel is GovX, where Norton 360 with LifeLock is offered at gated government/military member pricing (aggregators cite “up to 45% off,” but you should verify the exact price live).

Just as important: Norton runs public first-year promos of roughly 37–52% off that anyone can take — and in year one these often rival the gated price. The smart move is to compare the GovX price against today’s public first-year deal on the same plan, buy the lower, and set a renewal reminder because every path jumps at renewal.
This is an independent guide from NavyWeek. We are not affiliated with LifeLock, Norton, or Gen Digital, and Gen Digital controls the terms and can change them at any time.
j-crew-military-discount: Yes — J.Crew offers a 15% military discount, and it is a real, first-party program (not just a coupon-site rumor). The same 15% covers active-duty service members, veterans, retirees, reserve and National Guard, and qualified dependents, plus medical professionals and first responders. You verify once through SheerID, and the discount works both online at jcrew.com and in J.Crew and J.Crew Factory stores.

Here is the honest part most pages skip: J.Crew runs deep public sales — often 40% or more, sometimes with an extra-percent-off-sale code — for much of the year, and J.Crew only lets you use one code per order. So when a big sale is live, the public price usually beats the 15% military discount, and you cannot combine the two. When there is no real sale, the verified 15% is your best route.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with J.Crew; J.Crew sets and can change these terms at any time, so confirm the current offer on J.Crew’s site before you buy.
fox-one-military-discount: Does FOX One offer a military discount? No. FOX One — Fox’s live news and sports streaming app that launched in August 2025 — does not offer a military, veteran, first-responder, or student discount. It costs $19.99 a month or $199.99 a year, with a short free trial and rotating public promos, and there is no ID.me, SheerID, or GovX military verification at its checkout.

If you have seen "Fox gives veterans a free year," that is a different product — Fox Nation, Fox’s opinion, documentary, and entertainment service — which really does give active military and veterans their first year free, then 50% off renewals, verified through SheerID. It is a separate app from FOX One’s live news and sports, so do not expect the free year to apply to FOX One.

So how does a service member get FOX One for the least money? The honest answer is not a military code — it is the paths everyone can use: authenticate free if your cable, satellite, or live-TV package already carries FOX; claim the Verizon FOX One perk (as much as 3 months free, or a $10/month credit) if you are a Verizon customer; or take the annual plan at $199.99 (about $16.67/month), which saves roughly $40 a year over monthly. This is an independent guide; we are not affiliated with FOX One, Fox Corporation, Fox Nation, SheerID, or Verizon.
ihg-military-discount: Yes — IHG Hotels & Resorts (Holiday Inn, Holiday Inn Express, Crowne Plaza, Kimpton, InterContinental, Staybridge, Candlewood, Hotel Indigo and more) offers a real Military Leisure Rate: a minimum of 5% off the Best Flexible Rate (more at some hotels, based on availability) for US and Canadian active-duty, veterans, retired military, and their family members. It’s for leisure travel, you book it by selecting the Government/Military rate on IHG.com or the app, and you show a valid military or veteran ID at check-in.

Keep two things straight. First, the separate Government Rate is for official travel — government employees, military on orders, and contractors — and requires official ID or work orders at check-in; it’s not a general veteran vacation discount. Second, because the military minimum is only about 5%, IHG’s own member advance-purchase rates often beat it — so on locked-in dates, compare both and book the cheaper. Either way you still earn IHG One Rewards points.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with IHG; IHG sets and can change these terms at any time.
expedia-military-discount: Expedia advertises a discount on select stand-alone hotel bookings for verified members of the military and veteran community, redeemed through ID.me. Expedia’s own landing pages promote "10% off select hotels," while the coupon terms page we located states an 8% value on the pre-tax hotel price — so the exact percentage you receive may vary, and you should confirm the live figure inside the ID.me flow before booking.

The discount is not automatic. After verifying your status with ID.me, you receive a coupon code that you enter on Expedia’s checkout page. It works only on stand-alone, prepaid hotel reservations (not flight+hotel packages or pay-at-the-property bookings) and is limited to the first room on a booking.

This is an independent guide. We are not affiliated with Expedia. Expedia controls these terms and can change or withdraw the offer at any time; always confirm the current rate and rules on Expedia’s official pages and within the ID.me verification flow.
dixxon-military-discount: Dixxon Flannel Co. offers a military and first-responder discount verified through VerifyPass — confirm your status, get a one-time code, and apply it at checkout on dixxon.com. Independent military directories consistently report the rate at about 10% off.

The code is single-use (roughly one per 24 hours) and doesn’t stack with other codes or sale events. Since Dixxon runs frequent limited drops and holiday sales, compare the ~10% code against whatever’s on sale before you check out.
This is an independent guide and is not affiliated with Dixxon. Dixxon controls all terms and can change them at any time. Confirm the exact percentage shown after you verify.
adt-military-discount: Does ADT offer a military discount? Not directly. ADT LLC publishes no first-party military or veteran discount — nothing appears on ADT’s own deals page, and the fine print on the partner offer specifically excludes purchases made "directly from ADT LLC." What everyone calls the "ADT military discount" is actually an ADT Authorized Dealer offer, delivered through WeSalute (formerly Veterans Advantage), which has been ADT’s military-verification partner since 2009, and also through GOVX.

The verified deal is real and worth it if it fits your situation: $99 professional installation (down from a normal $199), a free starter equipment package worth roughly $125, and eligibility for a $100 Visa reward gift card — marketed as up to $914.90 in total setup savings. The catches: you must be a homeowner, a new customer, pass a credit check, and sign a new 3-year monitoring agreement, and the deal can’t be combined with other ADT promos.

This is an independent guide. We aren’t affiliated with ADT; ADT and its authorized dealers control the terms and can change them at any time. Always confirm the live offer with the dealer before you sign.
geissele-military-discount: Geissele Automatics does offer an official military discount — 10% off select products — and it’s more inclusive than most “duty-use” brands: it covers active-duty military, active-duty law enforcement, active first responders, and U.S. veterans. You register a Geissele account, verify your status directly with Geissele (a .mil or department email, or an uploaded ID/DD-214), and after 1–2 business days the discounted prices show up when you’re logged in. There’s no GovX or ID.me in the loop — Geissele checks you itself.

The honest catch: 10% is modest, it’s “select product” only, and it doesn’t stack — not with other codes, and not on top of sale prices. So the biggest savings at Geissele don’t come from the military discount at all. They come from Geissele’s public seasonal sales (Black Friday/Cyber Monday historically run up to ~50% on clearance and 20–40% across much of the catalog), which everyone gets and which the 10% can’t be added to. The winning rule is simple: if a Geissele sale is live, take the sale price; if not, verified buyers use the 10% on eligible products.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Geissele Automatics, and Geissele controls the discount terms, eligible-product scope, and verification and can change them at any time.
wrangler-military-discount: Yes — Wrangler offers a 10% military discount on wrangler.com, verified through ID.me and applied at checkout. It covers active-duty service members, veterans, retirees, Reserve/National Guard, and dependents, plus first responders, nurses, medical providers, and hospital employees.

Here is the honest part most pages skip: the 10% is often not your cheapest option. Wrangler runs frequent public sales (routinely up to ~50% off, plus recurring multi-pair jeans deals), and its core styles sell for less at Walmart, Amazon, and — tax-free — at the military exchanges. If a sale is running or you are buying basics, skip the discount and take the lower public price.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Wrangler; Wrangler sets and can change these terms at any time.
rock-auto-military-discount: Does RockAuto offer a military discount? No. As of July 14, 2026, RockAuto has no military or veteran discount — and no identity-based discount of any kind for any group. ID.me states plainly that it is "not aware that Rockauto offers Military discounts," and RockAuto’s own promotions page lists only manufacturer instant-savings promos and Wholesaler Closeout clearance — never a military, veteran, first-responder, senior, or student offer.

If you’ve seen "35% off RockAuto military codes" on coupon sites, they’re fabricated. RockAuto has no public promo codes at all and doesn’t even have a standard coupon field — the only codes it issues are targeted ones (a shopper-reported ~5% code emailed to past customers, plus car-club codes), entered in the "How did you hear about us" box at checkout.

That’s not the end of the story. RockAuto’s base prices routinely undercut chain-store retail by 20–50% on many lines — and when they don’t, two real military discounts exist at the parts counter: O’Reilly Auto Parts and Advance Auto Parts both give verified military customers 10% off in-store. This guide shows when each path actually wins. NavyWeek is an independent guide and is not affiliated with RockAuto, O’Reilly, or Advance Auto Parts; every company controls and can change its own terms.
dollar-car-rental-military-discount: Yes — Dollar offers military and veteran savings, but not as one flat “flash your ID” percentage. The clearest published benefit is a 5% VetRewards discount through Veterans Advantage (you enter a CDP code at booking), while ID.me Shop markets an “up to 25% off” Military & First Responder rate verified through ID.me/SheerID. Active-duty travelers on official orders get U.S. Government agreement rates with unlimited miles and free LDW/CDW.

Because the military lane isn’t always the cheapest, the real win is comparing it against a prepaid “Pay Now” rate and your Costco, USAA, or AAA rate on the same car and date, and taking the lowest. Only one rate code applies per reservation, so these are mutually exclusive buckets — not a stack.
This is an independent guide from NavyWeek. We are not affiliated with Dollar Rent A Car or Hertz Global Holdings, and Dollar controls the terms and can change them at any time.
burton-military-discount: Burton offers a genuine 20% military discount on burton.com, verified through SheerID. It is available to active-duty, veteran, and reservist personnel of the U.S. and Canadian Armed Forces (Military.com’s Burton listing also names retirees and Reserve/National Guard). You verify once through SheerID, get a one-time-use code, and can re-request a new code every 3 months. It works online at burton.com only — not in Burton Flagship or Outlet stores.

Here’s the honest part: Burton discounts hard on its own. An End-of-Season sale up to 40% and a Black Friday sale up to 50%, plus a year-round Clearance/Outlet channel, are routine — and because the 20% military code is full-price-only and can’t be combined with other percent-off discounts, during any sale of 20% or more you’re better off skipping your code and buying the public sale price. Ignore coupon sites advertising "30–50% off military codes"; the only verified military figure is 20% online via SheerID (not GovX, not ID.me).
This is an independent guide — we’re not affiliated with Burton or SheerID, and terms can change at any time.
kennywood-military-discount: Straight answer: yes, Kennywood has a military discount. You can buy a Military Admission ticket for $36.99 — roughly half the $74.99 gate price — online, and it covers you plus up to four guests, with a quick affiliation-verification step at checkout.

Even better in early July: Kennywood runs free Military Days each summer (July 1–5, 2026 this year). Active, retired, veteran, and reservist military get in free with a valid military ID at the gate, and can add up to four discounted guest passes at $34.99 each.

This is an independent guide — we’re not affiliated with Kennywood or Palace Entertainment, and the park can change prices and dates at any time. Confirm current terms at kennywood.com/buy-tickets before you go.
booking-com-military-discount: Does Booking.com offer a military discount? Not a dedicated one. Booking.com publishes no military or veteran rate on its hotel or car-rental site, it uses no ID.me, SheerID, GovX, or WeSalute military verification, and ID.me itself says it is not aware of any Booking.com military discount. So don’t chase a "Booking.com military promo code" — the ones aggregators advertise are generic public coupons, and the "call a number to verify at participating retail locations" claim is fabricated boilerplate (Booking.com is online only).

What actually saves you money: first, join Genius, Booking.com’s free loyalty program — you get 10% off participating stays the moment you create an account, rising to 10-20% at Levels 2 and 3, which you keep for life. Second, and usually the biggest win if you’re eligible: book through American Forces Travel, the Department of Defense’s official MWR leisure-travel site, which is powered by Priceline (a corporate sibling of Booking.com) and advertises up to 50% off hotels after a quick DoD ID check.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Booking.com, Priceline, or American Forces Travel; Booking.com sets and can change these terms at any time.
aquarium-of-the-pacific-military-discoun: The honest answer first: the Aquarium of the Pacific has no everyday online military discount code. Despite what coupon sites claim, there is no ID.me, SheerID, or GovX checkout on aquariumofpacific.org, and the Aquarium publishes no flat "10%–25% military discount."

What it does offer is genuinely good: free admission for veterans and active military (with a service ID) on Veterans Day — reserve online in advance, because capacity is limited — and discounted advance tickets through any MWR/ITT office on base the rest of the year.

If you do not have base access and it is not Veterans Day, your best move is not a "military code" — it is the Aquarium’s public AAA "visit on a Wednesday for up to 30% off" online deal, an authorized reseller, or a Go City bundle, all of which beat buying full price directly. This is an independent guide; NavyWeek is not affiliated with the Aquarium of the Pacific, which sets its own terms and can change them at any time.
zales-military-discount: Zales — "The Diamond Store," owned by Signet Jewelers — offers a 10% military discount to verified service members. It’s confirmed on Zales’s own website, verified through ID.me, and works both online at zales.com and in stores. Once ID.me confirms your status, you get a one-time code to use at checkout.

The important caveat: the 10% is a one-time, non-stackable offer. It can’t be combined with Zales’s "Buy More Save More" deals or other coupons, and it excludes a long list of items — all watches, clearance, pre-owned and custom pieces, loose stones, gift cards, repairs, and several designer collections. Because Zales runs frequent, deep sales (up to 50% seasonal events, up to 60% clearance, tiered "spend more save more" offers), a live sale often beats the 10% — and since they don’t stack, you take whichever is bigger.

Best move: on an eligible full-price piece with no better sale running, use the 10% ID.me discount and route your purchase through Rakuten for 2% cash back on top. This is an independent guide — we’re not affiliated with Zales or Signet Jewelers, and terms, prices, and exclusions can change at any time. Always confirm on zales.com before you buy.
shutterfly-military-discount: Does Shutterfly offer a military discount? No. There’s no military checkout on shutterfly.com, no SheerID or ID.me military verification, and no GovX storefront. ID.me’s own Shutterfly page says it plainly — “We’re not aware that Shutterfly offers Military discounts” — and Shutterfly has confirmed the same directly. Any “Shutterfly military discount 50% off” or “57% off in-store with military ID” you see on coupon sites is fabricated (Shutterfly is online-only and has no stores).

The good news: you don’t need one. Shutterfly runs deep public promo codes almost constantly — a SAVEMORE-style code recently gave around 50% off orders $49+ with no verification — plus unlimited free 4x4/4x6 prints in the app (just pay shipping) and free-gift welcome offers for new accounts. These public deals beat any military percentage. The one rule to know: Shutterfly lets you use only one code per order — codes never combine — so the whole game is picking the single best code for your cart.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Shutterfly, and Shutterfly can change its offers, codes, and terms at any time; promo codes rotate and expire frequently.
jersey-mikes-military-discount: Jersey Mike’s does not have a single national everyday military discount. Because every Jersey Mike’s is individually owned and operated, any everyday discount is set by the local owner — many participating stores give roughly 10–20% (often a flat 15%) with a valid military ID, but it isn’t advertised by corporate, isn’t guaranteed, and varies store to store. Call ahead or ask at the counter first, and note it usually can’t be combined with other offers.

What Jersey Mike’s does run brand-wide is a Veterans Day free sub (Nov 11) for veterans and active-duty service members — historically a free Regular sub you claim with an email-club code plus proof of service. That’s separate from any everyday discount, and it’s not the same as Jersey Mike’s March "Day of Giving," which is a Special Olympics charity fundraiser, not a discount.

The move that saves the most day to day is open to everyone: join the free Shore Points rewards program and use any live app deal. This is an independent guide — NavyWeek is not affiliated with Jersey Mike’s, and Jersey Mike’s (and each franchisee) can change terms at any time. Ignore any "Jersey Mike’s military discount 50% off" coupon-aggregator page; that percentage is fabricated.
ogio-military-discount: Yes — OGIO gives verified US military members 15% off their entire order at OGIO.com, confirmed with ID.me at checkout. It covers active-duty, veterans, reservists, and retirees, and OGIO extends the same 15% to nurses, first responders, and teachers.

Here’s the money-saving catch: the 15% can’t be combined with other promo codes, and OGIO’s standard 20%-off email welcome code for a first order is a bigger discount. On your first purchase, the welcome code usually beats your military discount. Save the 15% for repeat orders — or skip both when a deep seasonal sale is live and stack a cashback portal instead.

This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with OGIO or Topgolf Callaway Brands; OGIO sets the terms and can change them at any time. Confirm the current offer on OGIO’s official military-discount page before you buy.
chrysler-military-discount: Chrysler offers a real, official military benefit: $500 in Military Bonus Cash toward the purchase or lease of select new 2027 and 2026 Chrysler-brand vehicles — the Pacifica and Voyager minivans. It’s a flat dollar allowance, not a percentage discount, verified through SheerID and redeemed at a franchised US Chrysler dealer — there is no online code to enter.

The smart strategy is simple: claim the $500 and stack it on whatever public national, regional, or dealer incentive is running at the time, since Chrysler’s seasonal public offers are usually worth far more than $500 on their own. If you’re stationed or deployed overseas, compare the separate Military AutoSource program instead.

This is an independent guide, not affiliated with Chrysler or Stellantis. Chrysler controls the terms of this offer and can change them at any time — always confirm current details on Chrysler’s official military-incentive page before you buy or lease.
newegg-military-discount: Does Newegg offer a military discount? No. Newegg does not currently offer a military or veteran discount. It ran a Veterans-Day 10% off military promo code years ago, but that offer expired in 2018, and today Newegg’s ID.me store page lists no military discount — just email-signup deals. There is no active ID.me, GovX, or SheerID military verification for Newegg.

You may see coupon sites advertising a confident "Newegg military discount — 10% off," or even "up to 62% off military." All of it is stale or fabricated. The only real military offer Newegg ever ran was a Veterans-Day 10% code that expired November 11, 2018. Any "Newegg military promo code" you find today is either that dead 2018 code or a generic public coupon mislabeled as military.

That does not mean you overpay. Newegg’s real savings live in its deal engine — Shell Shocker flash sales, Daily Deals, combo deals, and mail-in rebates — and you can stack a cashback portal and rebates on top. This independent guide shows the maximum-savings path for a service member at Newegg, without a military rate that does not exist.

We’re not affiliated with Newegg, and Newegg controls its offers and can relaunch a military discount at any time. This reflects status as of the review date — always confirm current terms at checkout before you buy.
gamestop-military-discount: GameStop does have an official military discount: 10% off, in stores only, all year long. If you’re a service member, the real ways to save are the same as for everyone: book a group of 10+ on a weekday for 10% off, pick a lower-priced division (Catskills tandems start at $75 versus $115 at Boone), and watch your local division around Veterans Day, when some locations — such as Amador, CA — have historically run appreciation events. Ignore coupon sites promising "25% military" or "SAVEMORE 35%" codes: none is confirmed by Rail Explorers, and one "military" SheerID offer floating in search results actually belongs to a cosmetics brand, not Rail Explorers.
This is an independent guide — NavyWeek is not affiliated with Rail Explorers. Rail Explorers controls its pricing and can change or add offers at any time.
apple-music-military-discount: Does Apple Music offer a military discount? No. There is no standing military or veteran discount on the Apple Music subscription today. The popular "4 free months for military and veterans" deal was a limited-time 2021 promotion (verified via ID.me) that expired on August 1, 2021 — it is not available now, even though many coupon and military-discount pages still present it as if it were live.

Apple does run a military program — the Veterans and Military Purchase Program, roughly 10% off eligible Macs and iPads for verified service members — but that is a hardware discount. It does not discount Apple Music streaming.

The real ongoing discount on the Apple Music subscription is the Student plan: $5.99/month versus $10.99 for Individual, for up to 48 months, with Apple TV+ included — verified through UNiDAYS (or SheerID in-app). That is open to enrolled college students, which includes many junior service members and veterans studying on the GI Bill. If you are not a student, check whether your wireless carrier bundles Apple Music for free, or whether Apple One undercuts buying services separately.

This is an independent guide — we are not affiliated with Apple, and Apple controls its pricing and offers and can change or revive promotions at any time. Prices ($10.99 Individual / $5.99 Student) can change; always confirm current terms on apple.com before you subscribe.
epic-pass-military-discount: Vail Resorts runs one of the deepest military discounts anywhere: the Epic Military Pass, a full unlimited, blackout-free season pass to Vail, Breckenridge, Park City, Keystone and its other owned resorts for a small fraction of the ~$1,089 retail Epic Pass. For the 2026/27 season the spring price was $215 for active-duty, Guard, Reserve, and retired members and their dependents, and $620 for veterans.

Eligibility is verified per person through SheerID right inside checkout. Active members with current orders or an LES often verify instantly; veterans may be asked to upload a DD214 or VA card. Note that military ID cards are not accepted as proof.

NavyWeek is an independent guide and is not affiliated with Vail Resorts or Epic Pass. Vail Resorts sets and can change all pricing and terms; the spring low price ends around May 25 each year, so confirm the current number at checkout.
texas-de-brazil-military-discount: Yes — Texas de Brazil offers a year-round 10% "Heroes’ Discount" on dine-in lunch and dinner (salad-area-only included) for active military, veterans, law enforcement, firefighters, nurses, EMS, and teachers. You show a badge or ID at the table — there’s no online code and no ID.me or GovX account to set up. It’s capped at 4 people per table and can’t be combined with other offers or white gift cards.

But the 10% is often not your cheapest option. If you’re a party of one or two, a first-time eClub 25% welcome certificate saves more; if you eat here regularly, the VIP Club ladder climbs from 25% to 50% (after your 3rd visit) to 100% off (after your 5th); and on Veterans Day and Memorial Day, the brand has historically run 25%–50% off dinner. None of these stack, so you pick the biggest one.
This is an independent guide. We’re not affiliated with Texas de Brazil, and the brand can change these terms at any time — verify at the restaurant before you order.
sun-outdoors-military-discount: Sun Outdoors (part of Sun RV Resorts / Sun Communities) offers a genuine military discount you can use yourself, with no verification portal needed. With promo code SALUTE, current and former U.S. and Canadian military members get 20% off select short-term RV stays, tent sites, and vacation rentals — or $200 off a new seasonal or annual stay. You add the code when you book online (or call 888-886-2477 for seasonal/annual) and simply show proof of military service at check-in.

The fine print matters: SALUTE can’t be combined with any other offer, promotion, or Sun’s weekly/monthly rates; blackout dates and site-type limits vary by resort; a minimum number of nights (up to 14) applies; the $200 credit is a one-time deal for new long-term guests; and the current promotion expires December 31, 2026. Because it can’t stack, always compare the 20% code against any live public sale or Sun’s own weekly/monthly rate and take the single best.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Sun Outdoors, which controls these terms and can change them at any time.
general-motors-military-discount: Yes, General Motors runs an official military discount — the GM Military Appreciation Program — that gives eligible active-duty members, reservists, National Guard, veterans, retirees, and a sponsored spouse a set "program price" below MSRP on a new Chevrolet, Buick, GMC, or Cadillac. You verify your status through ID.me, get an authorization number, and bring it to a participating dealer.

The catch most pages will not tell you: GM does not publish a percentage or dollar amount. It is a fixed, no-haggle price that changes by model, and GM’s own terms only say the offer is "not available with some other offers." That makes the program a guaranteed ceiling, not automatically the lowest possible number. The smart play is to lock your authorization number, ask the dealer which current national incentives stack on your exact vehicle, and compare the program price to a hard-negotiated deal on high-incentive models.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with General Motors. GM controls the program and can change its terms, eligibility, and eligible-vehicle list at any time.
daniel-defense-military-discount: Yes — Daniel Defense offers a real military and first-responder discount through its MILE Program (Military, Law Enforcement & Emergency personnel), verified with VerifyPass. As of mid-2026 the stated rate is 20% off at the Daniel Defense webstore for active duty, veterans, retirees, police, fire, EMT, and government employees. Register an account, click VERIFY on your Account Dashboard, and once you clear you are added to the MILE Customer Group and the discount applies automatically.

There is now a second official path: since June 2026, Daniel Defense’s full catalog is available through the Brownells VALOR program (verified via ID.me), which — unlike the MILE page’s published copy — explicitly covers military spouses and surviving spouses. If you qualify yourself, MILE’s 20% is usually the cleaner win; if you qualify through a spouse or want Daniel Defense in one cart with a thousand-plus other brands, VALOR is worth verifying first.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Daniel Defense or Brownells; they set and can change these terms at any time.
feetures-military-discount: Straight answer: yes — Feetures gives all military service members 10% off, but it is an email-based discount, not a verification-portal offer. Per Feetures’ own FAQ, you email hello@feetures.com and they send you a code for 10% off your order.

Two honest caveats. First, 10% often is not the best deal available: first-time buyers get a 15% welcome code, and Feetures bundles and sales can save more — and because Feetures allows only one coupon per order, you have to pick the single best one. Second, despite what some coupon sites claim, Feetures does not publish a first responder, nurse, teacher, or student discount, and there is no "20% via VerifyPass" program.
This is an independent guide — we are not affiliated with Feetures, and terms can change at any time. Confirm current details at feetures.com/pages/faqs.
public-storage-military-discount: Public Storage does not publish a first-party military or veteran discount. Its "Military Storage" page describes storage for deployments and PCS moves, and its veterans blog is a tribute to employees plus the same $1-first-month promotion that any new customer can get. The "up to 50% off" military offer you’ll see on coupon sites and WeSalute is the company’s public first-month promo — not a special military rate — and the WeSalute version sits behind a paid membership, so it usually costs you more than just booking online.

The smart move for a service member is simple: book the public $1-first-month or 50%-off deal directly at publicstorage.com (online web prices beat walk-in). Then, if you deploy or PCS, know the protections that are uniquely yours — not a discount, but the law. Under the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act, a storage facility cannot auction or foreclose on your stored belongings during your military service (and for 90 days after) without a court order, and PCS or 90+ day deployment orders let you end a term lease with no early-termination penalty.

This is an independent guide. We aren’t affiliated with Public Storage; Public Storage controls its promotions and can change them at any time, and SCRA rights are governed by federal statute, not by us — the summaries here are general information, not legal advice.

vivid-seats-military-discount: Vivid Seats offers a military discount of 10% off, capped at $30 per order, verified through ID.me — and the same terms extend to nurses, first responders, teachers, students, and other ID.me communities. This is an independent guide from NavyWeek. We are not affiliated with Vivid Seats, and Vivid Seats controls and can change these terms at any time — confirm current details at checkout before you buy.

specialized-military-discount: Specialized offers a genuine military discount through its Hero Pro Program, verified with ID.me. Specialized states it on its own Hero Pro page: it has partnered with ID.me to give active military, military spouses and dependents, veterans, first responders, nurses, and teachers access to a members-only portal. ID.me’s Specialized store page publishes the figure — 15–30% off bikes and 30% off equipment — though the exact percentage for your order is revealed once you log into the portal.

mdt-military-discount: The MDT military discount is real but low-key: MDT — the Canadian-founded precision-rifle chassis maker behind the ORYX, XRS, and ACC — gives military and law enforcement 10% off, but you won’t find a verification widget at checkout. Per MDT’s own help center, you email support@mdttac.com and they send you a 10% discount code. No ID.me, SheerID, or GovX is involved, and MDT doesn’t publish who exactly qualifies or what documents to send — that’s handled in the email exchange.

One timing note before you use that code: MDT runs exactly one sale a year — Black Friday — when everything on the site is discounted at varying depths and factory seconds and overstock go up for grabs. If you’re buying in late November, check the sale price against your 10% code first.

This is an independent guide; NavyWeek is not affiliated with MDT, which controls these terms — the code is issued case-by-case by its support team — and can change them at any time. Always confirm at the official policy page before you buy.
2nd-swing-military-discount: Does 2nd Swing Golf offer a military discount? The straight answer: 2nd Swing does not have a year-round, storewide military discount. ID.me confirms it is not aware of one, and there is no GovX or SheerID service tier on 2ndswing.com.

What exists is more specific. 2nd Swing’s “military discount” page mainly promotes the PING Military Rebate — a PING manufacturer mail-in rebate ($10–$30 per eligible PING club) that 2nd Swing helps you file. And around military holidays, 2nd Swing runs a form-gated “extra 10% off used clubs” promo (its Memorial Day 2026 offer started May 21 and excludes new and custom-order clubs).

The biggest savings, though, come from what 2nd Swing does best: used/pre-owned clubs (often 30–70% off retail) and its trade-in program — both of which beat any 10% badge. This is an independent guide; we are not affiliated with 2nd Swing Golf or PING, and terms change, so confirm current offers at 2ndswing.com before relying on them.
four-seasons-military-discount: Does Four Seasons offer a military discount? Straight answer: Four Seasons Hotels & Resorts does not have a military or veteran discount. There is no ID.me, GovX, SheerID, or "military rate" on fourseasons.com. The only military-labeled deal tied to the Four Seasons name is a 10% discount on vacation packages booked through American Airlines Vacations, verified by WeSalute — an air+hotel package offer, not a room-rate program.

Watch out for a common mix-up: the "Lodge of Four Seasons" in Lake Ozark, Missouri, advertises a military discount, but that is a separate, unaffiliated resort — not the luxury Four Seasons chain. For an actual Four Seasons stay, service members usually save more by booking the Best Available Rate through Amex Fine Hotels + Resorts or a Virtuoso travel advisor — the same rate, but with resort credits, free breakfast, upgrades, and a free 4th night — or by checking American Forces Travel.

This is an independent guide — NavyWeek is not affiliated with Four Seasons, and offers change. We explain the real best-value paths, who the AA Vacations package offer covers, the "Lodge of Four Seasons" confusion to avoid, and link straight to the sources so you can confirm current terms before you book.
cinemark-military-discount: Cinemark offers a military discount on movie tickets at participating theatres. To get it, bring a valid U.S. Government-issued military ID to the box office — Cinemark lists active duty, active reserve, retired, and dependents as eligible. The discount excludes special engagement films and events.

Cinemark does not publish a set percentage or dollar amount for this discount. The company states that pricing and participation vary by location and tells guests to check their local Cinemark theatre. Any "10%" or "25%" figure you see on coupon sites is not confirmed by Cinemark and may not match your theatre.
This is an independent guide, not affiliated with Cinemark. Cinemark sets and can change these terms at any time; verify with your local theatre before you buy.
enterprise-car-rental-military-discount: Enterprise Rent-A-Car offers the military community a verified, standing discount — but it is a government rate, not a headline "veteran percentage." On Enterprise’s own site, Government Leisure Travel gets 5% off base rates, and that leisure discount is open to current federal employees, active-duty members, retired employees, and veterans, with no military-association membership required.

If you are traveling on official orders or TDY, you use a different program: Enterprise is a participating vendor on the U.S. Government Car Rental Agreement, offering contracted government rates that bundle unlimited mileage in the continental U.S. (or Canada), physical-damage and third-party liability protection, and a full tank of gas at pickup. Enterprise does not publish this rate as a percentage or dollar figure — you price it live.

There is no ID.me, SheerID, or GovX gate — verification is a physical military ID, your official orders, or a government-issued credit card at the counter. Because the leisure discount is a modest 5%, it is worth price-comparing it on your dates against a USAA member rate, your Enterprise Plus rate, and any live public sale.

This is an independent guide to help you use the offer. We are not affiliated with Enterprise, and Enterprise controls the rates and terms and can change them at any time. Always confirm details on Enterprise’s official site before you book.
cricut-military-discount: Straight answer: yes. Cricut offers U.S. military and veterans a real, standing discount — actually two. There is an everyday discounted price on four machines (Joy Xtra $149, Explore 4 $249, Maker 4 $379, Venture $599) and an additional 15% off Cricut materials and accessories with free shipping on your whole order.

You verify through gocertify — not ID.me — and Cricut emails a discount code you apply in cart. The 15% is materials-only: it excludes machines, extensions, bundles, bulk, Protection Plans, and anything launched in the last 90 days, and the offer isn’t combinable with other promos. This is an independent guide; we’re not affiliated with Cricut, and Cricut can change these terms at any time.
safariland-military-discount: Safariland offers a 15% military and first-responder discount on orders at Safariland.com, verified through GovX ID. It is open to current and former U.S. military, their spouses and dependents, first responders (law enforcement, fire, EMS), and government employees. Verify once, get a single-use code, and apply it at checkout — one code per day.

But 15% off the sticker is not automatically the best you can do. Verified industry and law-enforcement professionals can unlock deeper ExpertVoice pro pricing, third-party dealers like OpticsPlanet often take about 20% off with no verification at all, and authorized shoppers can buy Safariland holsters tax-free at the Exchange. The smartest move is to compare the 15% direct price against those before you check out.
This is an independent guide — NavyWeek is not affiliated with Safariland. Safariland sets the terms and can change them at any time.
otterbox-military-discount: Straight answer: OtterBox does not offer its own military or veteran discount. Its website has no ID.me, GovX, or SheerID military checkout, and ID.me itself says it is "not aware that OtterBox offers Military discounts." So ignore the coupon sites promising "25% off via ID.me at checkout" — that offer isn’t real.

What does save money for service members: if you can shop the military exchange (AAFES/NEX), OtterBox is stocked there tax-free, including current iPhone Defender cases. If you own an older iPhone or iPad, GovX gives verified military, veterans, first responders, government workers, and teachers up to 25% off the (mostly older-model) cases it stocks. Approved ExpertVoice members can access gated pro pricing. And for everyone, OtterBox’s own 20% first-order email code and buy-2 "35%" multi-buy usually beat every "military" claim on a current-model case.
This is an independent guide — NavyWeek is not affiliated with OtterBox, ID.me, GovX, or ExpertVoice, and any brand can change its terms at any time.
xfinity-military-discount: Xfinity’s military offer isn’t a coupon or a percentage off — it’s a package of perks for verified service members and their families who have Xfinity Internet. Verify your military status at xfinity.com/military and you can get a free Xfinity Mobile line (Mobile Select) for 2 years, an instant upgrade to Diamond (Xfinity’s top membership tier, which includes Peacock Premium at no extra cost), and NOW TV free for 1 year with 125+ live channels.

The benefits are layered onto Xfinity Internet service — Xfinity Mobile requires Xfinity Internet, and the free Mobile line is included with it. Eligibility is broad: active and reserve members, retirees, veterans, reservists, Gold Star families, and household spouses and family members all qualify. Heads up: you may still see older pages advertising a "$50 prepaid card" — that’s no longer Xfinity’s military offer.

This is an independent guide to help you use the offer. We’re not affiliated with Xfinity or Comcast, and Xfinity controls the terms and can change them at any time. Always confirm details on Xfinity’s official military page before you buy.
greyhound-military-discount: The Greyhound military discount is real — 10% off base fares — but it runs through WeSalute (formerly Veterans Advantage), and it requires a paid WeSalute+ Card. Once you have the card, you book on greyhound.com or the app by choosing "WeSalute" as the passenger type and entering your WeSalute+ Travel Code, then show the card when you board.

The catch: the 10% covers only the base fare (not service fees), can’t be combined with other Greyhound promotions, and only makes financial sense if you ride often enough to cover the annual membership fee. Occasional riders usually do better with Greyhound’s advance-purchase fares and public promos, which you can’t stack with the WeSalute rate anyway.

This is an independent guide — we’re not affiliated with Greyhound or WeSalute, and either company can change the rate, the terms, and the membership fee at any time. Confirm the current details on the WeSalute Greyhound page before you buy.
sig-sauer-military-discount: SIG SAUER does support the military and first-responder community — but the savings come in three different programs, and knowing which one to use is the whole game. The everyday online offer is 15% off all non-sale items on the SIG webstore, verified through VerifyPass — but it excludes firearms, suppressors, and sale items, so it is for accessories, optics, apparel, magazines, and ammo, not the gun itself.

To save on an actual firearm, you use SIG’s OFF-DUTY program: special program pricing on select pistols and rifles, redeemed through participating OFF-DUTY or SIG Law-Enforcement/Military dealers — an FFL, not your doorstep. A standard P365 runs roughly $449.99 under OFF-DUTY versus about $499 street. The deepest tier, up to ~30% off, is the SIG Professional Program for armed professionals (sworn law enforcement, agencies, instructors), which was extended to honorably discharged veterans in 2023.

Ignore the coupon sites promising "30% off any SIG online for all veterans" — that conflates the programs, and firearms are never part of the 15% webstore code. This is an independent guide; we are not affiliated with SIG SAUER or VerifyPass, and SIG controls the terms and can change them at any time.
red-wing-military-discount: Red Wing offers a verified military and veteran discount online through ID.me — a flat $15 off each pair of boots and shoes for military, veterans, first responders, nurses, medical providers, hospital employees, and teachers (students get 15% instead). You verify with ID.me at checkout on redwingshoes.com and the discount applies automatically. It is online only, cannot be combined with other offers, and excludes sale items and collaborations.

Two paths often beat that coupon. If your job requires safety-rated boots, ask whether your employer runs a Red Wing For Business program — employer-funded vouchers can cover most or all of the cost. And because Red Wing rarely marks down its heritage footwear, a local store that honors an in-store military discount (about 10% is commonly reported) can save more than the online $15 on a pricier boot — but that is a store-by-store policy, so call ahead.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Red Wing. Red Wing controls the terms and can change them at any time.
graco-military-discount: Does Graco offer a military discount? No. Graco’s own Help Center says it "does not offer a specific military discount at this time," and ID.me confirms it is not aware of any Graco military offer — Graco is not on ID.me, GovX, or SheerID. The coupon-site headlines you may have seen ("up to 38% off," "40% off," "HONEY10 for 20% military") are not real military benefits; HONEY10 is just a generic public code anyone can use. (This is Graco Baby, gracobaby.com — the baby-gear brand, not the industrial-pump company.)

The one genuinely military-tied way to save on Graco is the military exchange: AAFES (shopmyexchange.com) and the Navy Exchange (mynavyexchange.com) both stock a wide range of Graco car seats, strollers, and travel systems tax-free with free shipping for eligible shoppers — on a $300+ car seat, skipping sales tax alone is worth roughly $20–30. For everyone else, the best deals are Graco’s own frequent ~20% car-seat sales, its 20%/15% email-signup code, the BUNDLE3 25%-off-three code, and ~2% cashback.

This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Graco or Newell Brands, and Graco sets and can change its own terms at any time. We link straight to Graco’s Help Center and the exchanges so you can confirm the current terms before you buy.
field-museum-military-discount: The Field Museum in Chicago offers free general admission to active-duty military, veterans, and Illinois Gold Star ID cardholders, plus discounted tickets for up to six military family members. Show a valid military status ID at the ticket counter — there’s no online military rate.

If you’re active-duty and visiting in summer, the museum also participates in Blue Star Museums (May 16 – September 7, 2026), which gets you and up to five family members in free. General admission is what’s covered; special exhibitions or All-Access upgrades may cost extra.
This is an independent guide and is not affiliated with the Field Museum. The museum controls all terms and can change them at any time.
citi-military-discount: Citi doesn’t offer a "military discount" — no code, no percent off. What it offers is governed by federal law and is worth far more. Under the Military Lending Act (MLA), active-duty servicemembers and their spouses get Citi annual fees refunded to $0 on consumer cards opened while they serve — on the $595 Citi Strata Elite the credit is reported to post automatically, no paperwork. Under the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act (SCRA), accounts opened before active duty get reduced interest — the law caps it at 6%, and Citi is widely reported to go to 0% — plus fee relief, and Citi accepts requests up to a full year after you leave active duty.

Which law applies comes down to one thing: when you opened the card. During covered service (and on or after October 3, 2017) → MLA, automatic on the Strata Elite or by a quick email on older cards. Before service → SCRA, by request. Neither touches your points, miles, welcome bonus, or lounge access.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Citi; Citi sets its card terms and can change them, and eligibility is defined by federal law and Department of Defense records.

This is an independent guide, not affiliated with Tecovas. Tecovas controls the offer and its terms and can change them at any time — always confirm the current details on Tecovas’s official military discount page before you buy.

vw-military-discount: Volkswagen’s Military and First Responders Bonus puts a flat $500 toward the lease or finance of a new VW — and it is one of the more inclusive auto programs: active duty, veterans within 24 months of discharge, retirees, first responders, and their household family members all qualify.

hawaiian-airlines-military-discount: Hawaiian Airlines does not publish a percentage off airfare for military travelers. What it offers directly is a checked-bag fee waiver: active-duty members and qualified dependents traveling on official orders get their first 5 bags free (up to 70 lb each), and on personal or leisure travel active-duty members get 2 free bags (up to 50 lb each). You claim it in person at airport check-in with a military ID and proof of orders — there is no online military-fare portal.

The only actual fare percentage comes from outside Hawaiian: 5% off economy fares through a paid WeSalute (formerly Veterans Advantage) VetRewards membership, which now covers both Alaska and Hawaiian, year-round, for up to six people on a booking — worth it only if you fly enough to beat the membership fee.

Heads-up on timing: Alaska Airlines has acquired Hawaiian.
