Traeger grills are also stocked tax-free at the military exchanges (AAFES and Navy Exchange), and Home Depot and traeger.com run frequent seasonal markdowns ($100–$300 off at Black Friday).

During a deep sale, or for an exchange-eligible shopper, those routes can beat the ID.me discount — and none of them stack, so buy whichever is lowest all-in. This is an independent guide — we’re not affiliated with Traeger, ID.me, the military exchanges, or any retailer, and terms can change at any time.
comcast-military-discount: Does Comcast offer a military discount? Here’s the honest short answer: Comcast’s consumer services are sold under the Xfinity brand, and the military benefit is the Xfinity offer. There is no separate flat "Comcast" percentage or coupon — Comcast Corporation’s own military page directs service members to xfinity.com/military.

The Xfinity benefit is a perks bundle, not a bill discount: verified service members and military families who have Xfinity Internet get a free Xfinity Mobile line for 24 months, NOW TV free for a year, and an automatic upgrade to Diamond Rewards, which includes Peacock Premium at no extra cost. Because those perks belong to Xfinity, NavyWeek covers them in full on our Xfinity Military & Veteran Discount page.

This independent guide adds the parent-company picture that a pure "Xfinity discount" page misses: Comcast also runs Internet Essentials low-cost broadband (as low as $14.95/month) that many military families qualify for, a standalone Peacock military rate ($3.99/month for a year), and Universal Destinations military pricing through its NBCUniversal side. We’re not affiliated with Comcast, Xfinity, or NBCUniversal, and we link straight to the official pages so you can confirm the current terms before you buy.
mgm-military-discount: MGM Resorts runs a first-party Military & Veterans Program (MVP). The core benefit is 10% off standard room rates at MGM properties — booked on MGM’s own military-offers page and honored when you show a valid military or veteran ID at check-in. There is no ID.me or GovX step; you book the rate online and verify with your ID in person. The program also includes 25% off spa and salon services, about 10% off select dining, and — the part most people overlook — automatic MGM Rewards Pearl status, which brings free self-parking and a 10% Slot Dollars bonus.

Here is the honest part: 10% off a room is modest. For the room itself, a direct competitor — Caesars Entertainment, which offers up to 15% off its lowest rate via ID.me — often beats it on the same dates, so it is worth price-checking both. The two things that make MGM’s program genuinely worth using are the permanent-feeling Pearl perks (free self-parking can outrun the 10% on a short stay) and the fact that MGM’s rate is a plain online booking with no verification gate, so you can stack a cashback portal (Rakuten was ~3% as of June 2026) and a card-linked offer on top of it.

Ignore coupon sites framing MGM as "up to 25% off" for military: the 25% is the spa discount, not the room rate. This is an independent guide — we are not affiliated with MGM Resorts, and MGM controls the terms and can change them at any time.
cold-stone-military-discount: Cold Stone Creamery does not have a corporate military discount. Because every Cold Stone is independently franchised, each owner decides its own discounts — so a military benefit is up to your local store. Some stores offer a standing courtesy of around 10%, and a number offer a free scoop or discount on Veterans Day, but none of it is guaranteed.

Ignore the “30% off” or “50% off” claims on coupon sites — those reflect what one store did, not a chain-wide rate. The most dependable way to save is My Cold Stone Club, the free rewards program: you get a sign-up bonus and earn points on every dollar, good at participating locations. If you want a military rate, just ask your store and bring a military ID.
This is an independent guide from NavyWeek. We are not affiliated with Cold Stone Creamery. Franchise terms vary and can change at any time — confirm with your specific store.
bpn-military-discount: Short answer: yes — BPN (Bare Performance Nutrition) gives verified military members 15% off sitewide. Verify once through ID.me on BPN’s military-discount page and a one-time code applies at checkout; active-duty members, veterans, and dependents in the US and Canada qualify, and law enforcement, firefighters, and EMT/EMS get the same 15% through the first-responder page. BPN is a veteran-owned brand — founder Nick Bare is an Army veteran — and the discount is official and published, not manager’s-discretion.

The catch is BPN’s strict no-stacking policy: one discount per order, no military discount on subscription carts, and it’s switched off during major sales. That means the 15% is often not your best price — BPN’s Summer Sale (30% off all products, live as of July 13, 2026) and its 25%-off-new-subscriptions promo both beat it. Use the 15% on ordinary weeks; skip it whenever a bigger public discount is live.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with BPN; BPN sets and can change these terms at any time — confirm at bareperformancenutrition.com before you buy.
etsy-military-discount: Does Etsy offer a military discount? Not at the platform level. There’s no Etsy ID.me code and no site-wide service-member price break — Etsy is a marketplace of independent sellers, and each shop sets its own prices and coupons. The "Military Discount" pages on etsy.com are just search results for listings sellers chose to tag, not an official Etsy offer.

The way to actually save: message the shop directly and ask for a military/veteran coupon (many small and veteran-owned makers will oblige — it’s their call), watch for public Etsy sale events and shop coupons, and stack a cashback portal plus a rewards card on any order.
This is an independent guide. We’re not affiliated with Etsy, and Etsy and its sellers set and can change terms at any time. Always confirm current terms with the individual shop before you buy.
saks-military-discount: Saks Fifth Avenue does not offer a military or veteran discount, and neither does its outlet banner, Saks OFF 5TH. There’s no ID.me, SheerID, or GovX program on saks.com or in stores, and ID.me is "not aware" of any Saks military discount at either banner.

The widely reposted "Saks OFF 5TH 50% military discount, in-store, valid ID" is an aggregator fabrication — do not enter any "military code," because none is real. For a service member, the genuine savings paths are the public ones everyone uses.
This is an independent guide from NavyWeek. We are not affiliated with Saks, which sets and can change its programs at any time.
vivint-military-discount: Vivint doesn’t publish a flat percentage "military discount." Instead, military households get two real things: a contract-flexibility policy for deployed members (documented in Vivint’s Military Policy), and an active GovX offer — historically free professional installation plus your first few months of monitoring covered (up to about $399 in value) when you verify with GovX and call Vivint’s dedicated line using code GOVX4.

Because Vivint systems are custom-quoted by a rep over the phone, the smart move is to verify on GovX first, then call, and to get the deployment/PCS contract terms in writing before you sign. On-site "specials" (free $199 install, $0 activation, 24/7 monitoring from $44.99/mo) are the public default; the military add-on is the monitoring-months credit on top.

This is an independent guide. We’re not affiliated with Vivint, and Vivint controls the terms and can change them at any time — the GovX bundle and monitoring prices change frequently, so confirm before you buy.
truewerk-military-discount: The TRUEWERK military discount is 15% off through ID.me, and its eligibility list is unusually broad: active duty, veterans, National Guard and Reserve, retirees, military spouses and families, plus first responders, government employees, teachers, and students. Verification happens right at checkout with the green ID.me button, and the discount applies automatically once you’re verified.

One thing worth knowing before you verify: TRUEWERK also gives everyone 15% off their first order just for joining its email or SMS list. So on a first purchase, the military discount doesn’t beat the public one — its real value is that it works on every order after that, where the one-time welcome code doesn’t. And nothing stacks at TRUEWERK: it’s one discount per order, period.

This is an independent guide; NavyWeek is not affiliated with TRUEWERK or ID.me, and TRUEWERK controls these terms and can change them at any time. Always confirm the current offer on TRUEWERK’s official discount page before you buy.
deer-valley-resort-military-discount: Deer Valley Resort in Park City, Utah gives eligible U.S. military members an approximate 25% discount on lift tickets and season passes throughout the ski season, with military single-day lift tickets advertised at $189 for the most recent (25/26) winter. The discount covers active-duty, reserve, honorably discharged, and retired personnel plus their spouse and dependents 23 and under.

You verify your status through SheerID when you buy online, but there’s one rule that trips people up: every military ticket and pass is non-transferable and must be picked up in person at a Deer Valley ticket window, where you show a valid military photo ID. You cannot print a military lift ticket at a kiosk — even if you bought it online, you still stop at a ticket window so eligibility can be confirmed.

This is an independent guide to help you use the offer. We’re not affiliated with Deer Valley Resort, and Deer Valley controls the terms and can change them at any time. Pricing shown reflects the most recent published season — the 25/26 winter season has closed and 26/27 pricing is not yet published, so always confirm current-season rates on Deer Valley’s official military page before you buy.
nine-line-military-discount: Nine Line Apparel, a veteran-owned brand, offers 20% off non-sale items to military, first responders, medical workers/nurses, and teachers — verified through ID.me right at checkout. It is one of the cleaner offers in the category: verify once, get 20% on regular-priced gear.

The main limits are that it applies to full-price items only and cannot be combined with other codes or clearance pricing. During big sitewide sales, compare the sale price against 20%-off full price and take whichever is lower — they do not stack.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Nine Line Apparel, which controls the terms and can change them at any time; ID.me sets the verification rules.
gymreapers-military-discount: Yes — Gymreapers offers an official 10% military and first-responder discount on eligible gear. You verify your service status through the brand’s third-party verification partner, then apply your code at checkout. Eligibility is broad: active duty, retirees, veterans, and family members, plus first responders.

If a sitewide sale or public promo code of 10% or more is running, that public code is usually the better play, because the verified discount typically won’t stack with other codes. On full-price gear, the 10% verified discount is the clean win.

This is an independent guide. We’re not affiliated with Gymreapers, and Gymreapers sets and can change these terms at any time. Always confirm current terms on Gymreapers’ discount page before you buy.
disney-plus-military-discount: Disney+ offers a genuine military discount on its streaming service — 25% off the annual Disney+ Premium (No Ads) plan — but it works differently from most. You don’t redeem it on disneyplus.com. Instead, it’s an exclusive offer through The Exchange (AAFES) at ShopMyExchange.com, available to anyone authorized to shop there: active-duty service members, retirees, Guard and Reserve, honorably discharged veterans, and military families.

The offer is for new or eligible returning Disney+ subscribers only — if you already have an active Disney+ subscription, you can’t apply it to your existing account. It covers only the annual Premium (No Ads) plan, not the monthly plan, the ad-supported plan, or any Disney Bundle. The 25% discount continues at each yearly renewal off the then-current renewal price until you cancel.

This is an independent guide from NavyWeek. We are not affiliated with Disney+ or The Exchange. Disney controls the offer and can change or end it at any time; always confirm current terms on ShopMyExchange.com before subscribing.
chase-sapphire-reserve-military: Is the Chase Sapphire Reserve free for military? By consistent reporting, yes — the card’s $795 annual fee drops to $0 for active-duty servicemembers and their spouses, and not through a discount code. Open the card while you’re covered by the Military Lending Act (active duty, Guard/Reserve on 30+ day orders, or a military spouse or dependent) and Chase checks Department of Defense records at application, reportedly adjusts the fee to $0, and mails you a letter confirming it. It’s automatic; there is nothing to request. Editors report the $195 authorized-user fee is waived too.

One thing this guide says plainly that most don’t: Chase doesn’t publish any of this on chase.com. Its public pages cover the SCRA request process and its Military Services line (1-877-469-0110) — the $0-fee figure comes from Chase’s mailed benefit letters and years of consistent military-finance reporting, and we label it that way. Already had the Reserve before going on active duty? Then the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act is your route — request it, and Chase is reported to cut eligible balances to 4% APR and waive fees through active duty and up to a year after (the statutory floor is a 6% cap). Veterans and retirees no longer on active duty get no ongoing waiver — that’s the honest fine print.

This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with JPMorgan Chase; Chase sets card terms and benefit practices and can change them (it did in June 2025, raising the fee from $550 to $795), and eligibility is defined by federal law and Department of Defense records.
zumiez-military-discount: Does Zumiez offer a military discount? No. Zumiez publishes no military or veteran discount — and that’s not an oversight. The company states on its own site that it does not issue coupons or promo codes at all, and warns that "Zumiez coupons" you see on other sites "are not real." So any page promising a "15% Zumiez military discount" or a code like ZUMIEZSKATE09 is selling you something that doesn’t exist.

The good news: service members still have genuinely better ways to save on the same gear. If the brand you want — Vans, Nike SB, and other mainstream skate labels — is stocked at the military Exchange, you can buy it tax-free there. Otherwise, Zumiez runs sales and clearance every day (no code needed), the email list unlocks free-shipping offers, and the free Stash loyalty program builds reward value over time.

This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Zumiez, and Zumiez controls its own pricing and can change it anytime. We link straight to Zumiez’s official Deals page so you can confirm the current policy before you buy.
galls-military-discount: Galls sells uniforms, duty gear, and tactical equipment to public-safety professionals — but it does not run a verified military discount. There’s no ID.me, SheerID, or GovX gate. What people call the "Galls military discount" is really its "Unlock 15% Off" email/text signup code: you pick a profession from a dropdown (which even includes "Civilian") and get a 15%-off code — nothing checks your service.

That code works only on non-excluded brands (Galls excludes 5.11, Nike, Under Armour, Danner, Safariland, and many others from all promo codes), it’s one per order, and it can’t be combined with anything else. Because Galls almost always runs a public sitewide sale (up to 25% off as of July 18, 2026) that anyone can use without a code, the public sale or clearance price usually beats the 15% code — and you can’t stack them, so you take whichever is lower.

If you need an excluded premium brand, no Galls code helps at all — buy it on sale, on clearance, or through that brand’s own military offer. This is an independent guide; NavyWeek is not affiliated with Galls, and Galls controls the terms and can change them at any time.
halo-collar-military-discount: Does Halo Collar offer a military discount? The straight answer is no. Halo Collar does not publish a military, veteran, or first-responder discount, and it doesn’t use ID.me, GovX, or SheerID. Any "Halo Collar military discount" you’ve seen on a coupon site is just a public code relabeled for search — anyone can use it, and the advertised percentages are usually inflated.

The genuine discount is Halo’s standing on-site sale — currently $524 for the Halo Collar 5 (down from $599) — open to everyone. You can layer a cashback portal (Rakuten has listed roughly 10%; verify the live rate) on a code-free order, and check for any working public promo code at checkout. If you need two collars, the multi-collar bundle beats buying singles.

One thing to budget for: Halo’s GPS fence requires an ongoing Pack Membership (from $9.99/month) to work — that recurring fee, not the collar price, is the real long-term cost. This is an independent guide; we’re not affiliated with Halo Collar, and prices and codes change, so confirm current terms at halocollar.com before you buy.
swarovski-military-discount: Short answer: Swarovski does not offer a military, veteran, or first-responder discount right now. The company once ran a "Military and First Responder Discount" at checkout (verified through SheerID or ID.me) and a Veterans Day in-store 10% promo, but both have been discontinued — ID.me, the verification provider, confirms there is no active Swarovski military or first-responder offer as of July 15, 2026.

That does not mean you pay full price. Swarovski’s real savings come from its free Swarovski Club (10% welcome on your first order, 20% off in your birthday month), seasonal sales up to 40% off, and shopping-portal cashback (around 8% at the time of writing). Layered smartly, those beat the roughly 10% the retired military discount ever offered.
NavyWeek is an independent guide and is not affiliated with Swarovski. Swarovski sets and can change its own terms at any time.
aura-military-discount: Straight answer: yes. Aura — the digital-security and identity-theft-protection service at aura.com — offers a standing military discount of up to 52% off its protection plans, plus a two-week free trial, for the whole military community: active duty, retirees, veterans, reservists, National Guard, and their dependents.

You redeem it through Aura’s partnership with Military.com at buy.aura.com/military, where you confirm your military status in the offer flow. There’s no ID.me, SheerID, or GovX step. One thing to check at checkout: Aura’s pages don’t all agree on the exact number (its help center says up to 52%, its military landing page currently shows up to 68%, and the 2022 launch was 50% off the Family plan), so confirm the live discounted price before you pay.

Want the deepest cut? If you hold a WeSalute membership, Aura’s WeSalute partner offer advertises up to 75% off — compare it against the direct 52% offer net of WeSalute dues. This is an independent guide; we’re not affiliated with Aura, and Aura can change these terms at any time.
home-depot-military-discount: The Home Depot gives U.S. veterans, active-duty service members, and their spouses 10% off full-priced, non-appliance merchandise — every day, year-round, both in stores and online. You verify your status once through the Home Depot app or website, and your eligibility is saved to your Home Depot account. In store, you pull up a virtual ID QR code in the app and scan it at the register; online, the discount applies automatically at checkout when you’re signed in.

A few things to know before you shop: appliances are excluded from the 10% (though eligible military shoppers can buy many appliances tax-free through a separate Military Exchange program), and the discount applies to full-priced items. Independent military-benefit sites also widely report a $400 maximum annual discount and a list of other exclusions (clearance, gift cards, lumber and other commodities, labor, delivery, tool rental) — but The Home Depot’s official terms page is not publicly machine-readable, so confirm the current cap and exclusions on Home Depot’s own military page before counting on them.

This is an independent guide to help you use the offer. We’re not affiliated with The Home Depot, and The Home Depot controls the terms and can change them at any time. Always confirm details on Home Depot’s official military discount page before you buy.
petsmart-military-discount: PetSmart does not have a military or veteran discount on regular merchandise — there’s no "10% off pet food and supplies" offer online or in store, despite what some coupon sites claim. What PetSmart does offer are two service discounts, both 10% and both redeemed in person: 10% off Grooming Salon visits on Tuesdays, and 10% off any overnight PetsHotel stay.

There’s no ID.me, GovX, or online checkout step. You simply show ID to a Services associate at the salon or PetsHotel desk. For grooming, PetSmart’s eligibility is broad and explicit — Reserves, National Guard, active members of all five armed services, retired members, and their spouses — and it accepts an expired military ID or a DD214 as proof. A Treats Rewards membership (free) is required for the grooming discount. The PetsHotel discount also covers state and local first responders.

This is an independent guide to help you use the offer. We’re not affiliated with PetSmart, and PetSmart controls the terms and can change or end them at any time. Always confirm current terms with a store associate before you book.
progressive-military-discount: Progressive does not offer a nationwide military or veteran discount on car insurance. As of June 23, 2026, Progressive’s official auto discounts page lists no military, veteran, National Guard, or first-responder discount. If you’ve seen a "Progressive military discount" mentioned online, it almost always refers to one thing: a Louisiana law that requires every auto insurer in the state — Progressive included — to give a 25% discount on liability premiums to qualifying military residents.

That means the discount is a Louisiana statutory benefit, not a Progressive marketing program, and it does not exist in the other 49 states. Eligibility centers on Louisiana-resident active-duty members, reservists, and Louisiana National Guard. Veterans and retirees are not automatically entitled to it.

This is an independent guide. We are not affiliated with Progressive. Progressive (and Louisiana law) control the terms, which can change. Always confirm current details with Progressive or the Louisiana Department of Insurance before relying on them.
tarte-military-discount: Yes — Tarte Cosmetics offers a genuine 40% off military discount, one of the deepest identity discounts in beauty. It covers active duty, veterans, retirees, reservists, National Guard, and active-duty and Gold Star military families. You verify your status through SheerID on Tarte’s Special Offers page, and once approved you get a one-time-use code emailed at the start of each month to use at tarte.com.

Two things to know. First, it’s online only — despite what some coupon sites claim, there is no in-store "show your ID at the register" Tarte military discount. Second, it’s non-combinable: the 40% code can’t be stacked with other promo codes, sale offers, e-gift cards, loyalty rewards, or cashback, and it’s capped at $500 of eligible items per order. The good news is you rarely need to stack — at 40%, the military code beats Tarte’s public sales outright.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Tarte Cosmetics. Tarte controls its terms and can change them at any time; confirm current details on tarte.com before you buy.
peacock-military-discount: Peacock gives verified military members Peacock Premium for $6.99/month for 12 months — down from the standard $10.99/month. The discount covers active-duty service members, Reservists, National Guard members, veterans, and retirees who are 18 or older and live in the U.S. You verify your status through SheerID at peacocktv.com/military, get a unique one-time promo code, and apply it to a new or existing Peacock account.

Two things to know before you sign up: this is a 12-month promotional price, not a permanent rate — afterward your plan auto-renews at $10.99/month (or the then-current price) plus tax unless you cancel, and Peacock requires you to re-verify through SheerID each year to keep the discounted rate. You also need a valid payment method on file, since you are billed $6.99/month during the offer (it is not a free subscription).

This is an independent guide to help you use the offer. We’re not affiliated with Peacock or NBCUniversal, and Peacock controls the terms and can change or end them at any time. Always confirm current details on Peacock’s official military page before you enroll.
discovery-plus-military-discount: Does discovery+ offer a military discount? Not to new subscribers. discovery+ closed its military discount — 40% off the Ad-Lite plan, which brought it to $2.99/month, verified through SheerID — to new sign-ups on June 1, 2023. If you were already enrolled before that date, discovery+ honors your discounted rate for as long as you stay subscribed and remain eligible, but you cannot get back in once you cancel.

That means the "$2.99 discovery+ military" price still floating around coupon sites is stale: it is the pre-June-2023 offer, and new service members pay standard pricing ($5.99/month Ad-Lite, $9.99/month Ad-Free). There is no current ID.me or SheerID military checkout on discoveryplus.com.

So what is the real move today? If you want discovery+ itself, the annual Ad-Lite plan ($59.99/year, about $5/month) is the simplest genuine saving — roughly two months free versus paying monthly — and it is worth checking your wireless carrier’s perks, since plans like Verizon’s +play have bundled discovery+ for free. If you mainly want a streaming service with a standing military discount, Paramount+ gives verified military 50% off any plan for life. This independent guide lays out who is grandfathered, what to avoid, and every honest way to save.
margaritaville-cruise-military-discount: The Margaritaville cruise military discount is the most generous hero offer in the cruise industry: through Heroes Sail Free, GovX-verified U.S. service members, veterans, first responders, nurses, educators, and government employees get a $0 cruise fare for themselves and a second guest in an Interior stateroom on select sailings of Margaritaville at Sea’s Islander (Port Tampa Bay) and Paradise (Port of Palm Beach).

"Free" means free fare — you still pay taxes, fees, and port expenses per guest at booking (no flat figure is published; it varies by itinerary), plus gratuities and anything you buy on board. Free cabins are capacity-controlled and go first-come, first-served, so date flexibility is the real currency. If no free cabin fits your dates — or you want a balcony — verified heroes instead get an additional 20% off the best available retail fare. Verification runs through a free GovX membership.

This is an independent guide; NavyWeek is not affiliated with Margaritaville at Sea or GovX. Margaritaville at Sea controls the terms and can change them at any time — the program has been re-scoped before — so always confirm current terms on the official Heroes Sail Free page before you book. (Looking for Margaritaville resorts and hotels? That’s a separate brand with its own offer — see our Margaritaville resorts guide.)
beats-military-discount: Beats by Dre does not offer its own military discount. There’s no service-member program on BeatsByDre.com and no ID.me military offer on Beats’ own store. But because Beats is an Apple company, verified military members can buy Beats through Apple’s Veterans & Military Store for 10% off (verified via ID.me), or shop GovX for member pricing.

Honestly, the best price is usually a plain public sale: Beats headphones are marked down frequently — a Studio Pro that lists at $349.99 routinely drops to $199–$249 at Beats.com, Amazon, Best Buy, and Target. If you have base-exchange access, buying tax-free at the Exchange is another strong route. Compare all four before you buy.
This is an independent guide; we’re not affiliated with Beats or Apple, and terms can change at any time.
evenflo-military-discount: Yes — Evenflo offers a 20% military and veteran discount on evenflo.com through its Community Heroes program, verified with ID.me. Active duty, military dependents, veterans, reservists, and the National Guard all qualify, and the same 20% extends to first responders, healthcare workers, teachers, and college students. Second, if you’ve seen a "25% Evenflo military discount," that was a past Veterans Day promotion, not the everyday rate — today’s everyday offer is 20%.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Evenflo. Evenflo controls all pricing and terms and can change them at any time.
honda-military-discount: Honda’s military benefit is the Honda Military Appreciation Offer: $500 toward a new 2025-or-newer Honda when you finance or lease through Honda Financial Services (HFS). On a purchase it goes toward your down payment; on a lease it reduces the cap cost. It’s a flat $500 — not a percentage off — and it requires HFS financing with credit approval.

Eligibility is unusually broad for an automaker: active-duty military and Ready Reserve, veterans within two years of separation, retirees, the spouses of all those groups, and Gold Star family members. You prove eligibility with documents at the dealership — an LES, DD-214, Military ID, or Gold Star paperwork — there’s no online verification and no code to enter.
One $500 certificate applies per vehicle, and it combines with other HFS programs except the Zero Due at Signing Lease program. The offer runs through March 31, 2027, unless Honda ends it sooner.

This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Honda or Honda Financial Services. Honda and HFS control the terms and can change or end them at any time — confirm current details with a Honda dealer or HFS before you buy.
playstation-military-discount: Short answer: PlayStation does not offer a military or veteran discount. There’s no military pricing on the PS5, PS5 Pro, controllers, or PlayStation Plus, and PlayStation Direct’s deals page confirms it — the only listed savings are financing, trade-in, refurbished units, and a co-branded credit card. Don’t be fooled by pages citing a “Sony 15% military discount”: that’s Sony Electronics (TVs, cameras, headphones — a separate division), and it does not cover PlayStation.

On hardware, the real win is the military Exchange (shopmyexchange.com for Army/Air Force, mynavyexchange.com for Navy): PS5 consoles ship tax-free with free shipping for eligible buyers — active duty, Reserve, National Guard, retirees, honorably discharged veterans, dependents, and DoD/Coast Guard civilians — often below retail. This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with PlayStation or Sony; PlayStation sets and can change its pricing and programs at any time.
office-depot-military-discount: Office Depot and OfficeMax give the military community 20% off qualifying regular-price purchases in stores nationwide. Walmart’s position is that its "Everyday Low Prices" apply to everyone equally, and it doesn’t gate a military coupon behind ID.me, GovX, or any verification wall.

There is one military-relevant benefit worth knowing. Walmart+ Assist cuts a Walmart+ membership to 50% off — $49/year or $6.47/month instead of $98/year — and veterans and survivors who receive the VA "Veterans and Survivors Pension Benefit" qualify, verified through SheerID. It is needs/pension-based, not an all-veteran discount, and it applies to the membership only, not to products.

This is an independent guide. We’re not affiliated with Walmart, and Walmart controls its programs and can change them at any time. Always confirm current terms on Walmart’s official pages before relying on them.
alaska-airlines-military-discount: Alaska Airlines runs a "Salute to Service" program built around active-duty travel rather than a single percentage-off code. Active-duty service members and their accompanying spouse and dependent children get a phone-only special military fare, free checked bags (up to 5 on orders), 15% off inflight food, priority boarding, a discounted lounge day pass, and flexible changes when orders disrupt travel.

If you’re a veteran, retiree, or Guard/Reserve member not on active duty, you generally won’t qualify for the active-duty fare or perks. Your main fare-savings path is WeSalute+ (formerly Veterans Advantage), a paid third-party membership that unlocks 5% off Alaska and Hawaiian base fares through a private booking portal.

This is an independent guide. We are not affiliated with Alaska Airlines. Alaska controls all terms and can change them at any time; always confirm current details on Alaska’s official pages before booking.
ifit-military-discount: There’s no umbrella "iFIT military discount." iFIT is the app that runs on NordicTrack, ProForm, and FreeMotion machines — and only NordicTrack publishes a military discount: 5% off your entire order for current and former U.S. military, verified through GovX ID. ProForm offers no military discount, and the iFIT app subscription has no military price.

Here’s the honest part: NordicTrack machines go on sale constantly — often $200–$700 off — and that public sale almost always beats 5%, and the two usually don’t combine. So the best move is timing, not the code.
This is an independent guide — we’re not affiliated with iFIT, NordicTrack, or ProForm, and terms can change at any time. Confirm current offers at nordictrack.com before buying.
saks-fifth-avenue-military-discount: Saks Fifth Avenue does not offer a military or veteran discount. The off-price sibling Saks OFF 5TH is the same: ID.me Shop lists it but states it is "not aware" of any military offer there.

The "20% off," "40% off," and "50% off military" codes floating around coupon sites are not real Saks military discounts. They trace to no Saks primary source — most are ordinary public promo codes relabeled as "military." If a page asks you to "verify military status for a Saks discount," it is not an official Saks flow.

So the honest best way for a service member to save at Saks is exactly how everyone else saves: cashback through Rakuten, a seasonal sale or gift-card-with-purchase event, Saks OFF 5TH for off-price versions of comparable goods, and free SaksFirst points — plus the semi-annual Saks credit if you carry an Amex Platinum. This is an independent guide; we’re not affiliated with Saks Fifth Avenue, and Saks can change its terms at any time.
hurricane-harbor-military-discount: Six Flags Hurricane Harbor water parks offer a real military and first-responder discount — but it works differently from a percent-off coupon. You get fixed discounted prices (daily tickets from about $20, and a Military Gold season pass around $80 at many parks), redeemed online only after you verify with ID.me. It cannot be combined with other sales, and there is no military rate at the front gate.

If you will visit more than once, the Military Gold Pass is the standout value — it typically pays for itself in about two visits and adds free general parking. For a single trip, the discounted daily ticket (buy up to six for family and friends) is the move.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Six Flags; terms are set by Six Flags and can change at any time, and prices vary by park.

cycle-gear-military-discount: Cycle Gear offers a genuine military and first-responder discount, verified through GovX — but how much you save depends heavily on where you shop. In-store with ID, you get 20% off Cycle Gear’s exclusive house brands (SEDICI, BILT, Street & Steel) and 10% off third-party brands. The discount also will not stack with promo codes, sale prices, or Cycle Gear’s RPM rewards. So the best move is simple: buy house-brand gear in-store at 20% off. patagonia-military-discount: Does Patagonia offer a military discount? No. There is no active-duty, veteran, retiree, spouse, or dependent discount on patagonia.com, and Patagonia does not run an ID.me, SheerID, or GovX military verification program. Patagonia is unusual among outdoor brands in that it rarely discounts at all — its own coupons page asks shoppers to ignore any site claiming to offer Patagonia promo or discount codes.

You may see other websites advertising a "10% Patagonia military discount" or a "Veterans Day 10% off." We could not verify those claims against any Patagonia-owned page, and Patagonia’s official guidance is to disregard sites claiming to offer its discount codes. Treat those offers as unconfirmed.

There are still legitimate ways for service members and veterans — like everyone else — to save on Patagonia: year-round Web Specials (no code needed), used gear through Worn Wear, and a trade-in program. This is an independent guide; we are not affiliated with Patagonia, and Patagonia can change its policies at any time.
theragun-military-veteran: Does Theragun offer a military discount? Yes — a real one. Theragun’s parent brand, Therabody, gives 20% off full-price products to military, veterans, medical professionals, and first responders, verified for free through ID.me (students and teachers get a separate 10%). That puts it ahead of many brands that have no military rate at all.

But here’s the money-saving twist most coupon pages won’t tell you: Therabody discounts heavily and often. Black Friday 2025 hit 35% off, and trackers logged 50% peaks in December 2025 and March 2026 against a ~13% baseline. Because the 20% is "not combinable" and full-price only, during any 30%+ sale the public price beats your military discount outright — and the 20% can’t be applied to sale items. So the most important move on this brand is to time the purchase, not just grab the code.

That makes this a genuine multi-path decision: the direct 20% via ID.me, a deep seasonal sale plus cashback, the GovX storefront, or a certified-refurbished unit — and which one wins flips entirely with the time of year and whether you’re verified. Use the chooser and decision table below to find your best path; we link straight to the official sources so you can confirm the current terms before you buy.
chilis-military-discount: Chili’s Grill & Bar honors the military mainly through its annual free Veterans Day meal. On November 11, 2026, all veterans and active military members can choose a free entrée from a limited menu at participating Chili’s restaurants — dine-in only. Outside of Veterans Day, Chili’s does not advertise a nationwide everyday military or veteran discount; any in-store discount is at an individual location’s discretion, so call ahead before relying on one.

To redeem the Veterans Day meal, eligible guests dine in at a participating Chili’s on November 11 and order from the limited Veterans Day menu. The official page does not specify a required form of ID, but bringing valid proof of service (military ID, VA card, or DD-214) is prudent and may be requested at the restaurant’s discretion.

lancaster-archery-military-discount: Lancaster Archery Supply offers a 10% military discount on almost everything at lancasterarchery.com for active-duty, reserve, veteran, and retired US military. On regular-priced arrows, rests, sights, and accessories it’s a clean everyday saver; on MAP gear you’ll want the public Deals page instead.

This independent guide explains who qualifies, how the one-time VerifyPass verification works, and when the 10% actually wins — with a direct link to Lancaster’s official page so you can confirm the current terms before you buy.
carters-military-discount: Does Carter’s offer a military discount? Based on Carter’s public site, Carter’s does not publish a percentage-based military or veteran discount on carters.com. squarespace-military-discount: Squarespace does not offer a military or veteran discount. There’s no military checkout, no ID.me, SheerID, GovX, WeSalute, or VerifyPass military verification, and no military language anywhere on Squarespace’s official student-discount, coupons, or pricing pages.

If you’ve seen a "Squarespace military discount — 50% off" on a coupon site, that figure is a mislabeled version of Squarespace’s student discount — a real but separate program that takes 50% off the first year of an annual plan for currently-enrolled full-time college students, verified through Student Beans. If not, use a public code (a ~20% seasonal code when live, otherwise GIMME10 for 10%) on an annual plan; annual billing alone already runs ~28–36% cheaper than monthly. This is an independent guide; we’re not affiliated with Squarespace, and Squarespace can change its terms at any time.
hey-dude-military-discount: HEYDUDE gives verified military members and first responders 20% off full-price footwear and accessories, verified through ID.me at checkout on heydude.com. The brand is also listed on GovX as a second verification option. ID.me eligibility covers military, first responders, and more.

The honest catch: the 20% applies to full-price styles only — sale and collaboration styles are excluded. And HEYDUDE runs frequent public sales, which can beat 20% on the styles they cover. So verify once through ID.me for a standing 20%, but check the Sale section first — on discounted styles the public price usually wins (and the military discount wouldn’t apply there anyway).

universal-studios-orlando-military-disco: Universal Orlando Resort’s main military offer isn’t a coupon you enter online — it’s the 2026 Military Freedom Pass, a promotional ticket sold only through Authorized Military Ticket & Travel offices (your base ITT/MWR/Leisure Travel office, Shades of Green, and similar outlets). For a flat $220 (2-Park) or $255 (3-Park) per adult, an eligible service member gets more than a year of near-unlimited admission to Universal Studios Florida and Islands of Adventure — plus Volcano Bay on the 3-Park — from November 13, 2025 through December 18, 2026 (blockout dates apply).

Against Universal’s regular multi-day ticket prices, that’s an exceptional deal — it behaves like a heavily discounted annual-style pass, though Universal is explicit that it is not an Annual Pass and carries none of the AP perks. Two things to know: the brand-new Epic Universe park is not included (it’s a separately priced 1-Day add-on that requires an activated Freedom Pass), and the Freedom Pass is for active/retired military, Guard, Reserve, Coast Guard, spouses, DOD civilians, and 100% disabled veterans. If you’re a veteran who isn’t retired or 100% disabled, or a first responder, your path is GovX instead (up to $100 off, purchased online).

This is an independent guide — we’re not affiliated with Universal Orlando Resort. Terms, prices, and blockout dates change every pass year and ticket prices are dynamically priced, so always confirm at your base ticket office or on Universal’s official military page before you buy.
youtube-premium-military-discount: YouTube Premium does not offer a military or veteran discount. allen-edmonds-military-discount: Allen Edmonds offers a 15% military discount — 15% off one online purchase at AllenEdmonds.com — for active-duty service members, reservists and National Guard, veterans and retirees, military family members, and Gold Star families (US only). etrailer-military-discount: etrailer does not offer a military or veteran discount, and there’s no ID.me or GovX checkout gate. etrailer’s own answer is that it already prices low for every customer, so it doesn’t add a separate military discount on top — and the "up to 50% off military" claims on coupon sites are not real.

marriott-military-discount: Marriott offers special rates to the military community, but it works differently than a single coupon code. For everyday hotel stays, Marriott.com has a Government & Military rate you select under "Special Rates" (or by entering code GOV). This is an independent guide. We are not affiliated with Marriott. Marriott sets and can change all terms, and eligibility and availability vary by property — always confirm "Rate Details" for your specific hotel before booking.
olight-military-discount: Olight offers a 10% military discount for verified U.S. military members and veterans: you verify your status online through BeansID and the 10% applies while you’re logged in at olight.com. It’s a real, standing discount — but a narrow one. It can’t be combined with any coupon or promo code, and it doesn’t apply to Olight’s limited-time / flash-sale items, Members Area products, free bundles, or blind boxes.

Here’s the honest part: those excluded flash sales are where Olight’s best prices live. Olight runs deep site-wide sales and free-gift promos almost constantly, and they routinely beat 10% — and because the military discount can’t stack on a sale, the public deal is often the better buy. Use the 10% when you’re buying a full-price item that isn’t on a flash deal; otherwise take the sale, and cross-check GovX (a separate military marketplace that carries Olight).

hyatt-military-discount: Hyatt offers a genuine Veteran and Military Rate — 10% to 15% off the Hyatt Standard Rate — at participating Hyatt hotels and resorts in the US. You book it directly on hyatt.com using the Special Offer Code MILVET, and you show a valid US Military/Veteran ID or DD-214 at check-in. There’s no online ID.me step — it’s confirmed at the front desk. It’s open to veterans, active-duty members of any US branch, and their immediate family — parents, children/legal wards, spouses, and domestic partners — not just people on active orders. Separately, if you’re traveling on official government business, Hyatt’s Government rate (a per-diem-style rate for government employees and military) is bookable by selecting "Government" at booking and showing a government ID at check-in.

Here’s the honest part: hotel rates move constantly, and Hyatt’s AAA rate or Member Advance Purchase rate sometimes beats MILVET on a given night — these rates are mutually exclusive, so compare them and book the lowest. The one thing that genuinely stacks is Rakuten cashback (3% as of December 2025) layered on your booking. This is an independent guide to help you use the offer. We’re not affiliated with Under Armour, and Under Armour controls the terms and can change them at any time. Always confirm details on Under Armour’s official Military & First Responder FAQ before you buy.

1800-contacts-military-discount: Does 1-800 Contacts offer a military discount? No. 1-800 Contacts does not run a military or veteran discount, and there is no code to enter at checkout. That does not mean you have to overpay. The biggest lever is paying with an FSA or HSA card — pre-tax dollars that stack with any offer. And if you buy contacts regularly, a competitor that does run a real ID.me military discount — LensDirect at 20% off or ContactsDirect at 15% — will usually beat 1-800’s everyday price; alternatively, 1-800’s Best Price Guarantee will beat any lower public US price by $1.

This independent guide corrects the record on the fake military codes, walks through the paths that actually save on a year’s worth of contacts, and links straight to 1-800 Contacts’ and the substitute retailers’ official pages so you can confirm current terms before you buy.
dr-martens-military-discount: Dr. Martens does not offer a military or veteran discount. There’s no military offer on ID.me (which says it’s "not aware" of one), none through SheerID, and nothing on Dr. Martens’ own coupon page. If you’re a service member or veteran, the only way to get a Dr. Martens discount is to also qualify under a program the brand does run.

youtube-music-military-discount: Short answer: there’s no military or veteran discount on YouTube Music Premium or YouTube Premium — service members pay the standard $15.99/month. Veterans repeatedly ask in Google’s support forums, and the consistent answer is that none exists.
