Margaritaville Run Orlando gives 20% off registration via GovX, and individual restaurants run their own GovX and Veterans Day offers.

This is an independent guide — we are not affiliated with Margaritaville or GovX, and any brand or property can change its terms at any time, so confirm the current offer at the source before you book.
allbirds-military-discount: Yes — Allbirds offers a 15% military discount. You verify your status through GovX, and Allbirds issues a single-use promo code to use at checkout on allbirds.com. The same 15% is offered to healthcare workers, government employees, teachers, faculty and staff (all via GovX), and to students through StudentBeans.

The catch is in the fine print: the code is online-only in the US, limited to one per year, and can’t be combined with any other code. That matters because Allbirds runs frequent sales and keeps a standing outlet section that often marks shoes down more than 15% — and you can’t stack the code on top of a sale. So the best deal changes with the calendar: on a full-price staple the GovX 15% is the easy win, but when a deeper sale is live you’re better off just buying the sale price.

This is an independent guide. NavyWeek.org is not affiliated with Allbirds, and Allbirds controls the terms and can change them at any time. Always confirm current details on Allbirds’ Community Offers page before you buy.
timberland-military-discount: Timberland offers a genuine 10% military discount on timberland.com, verified through SheerID (not ID.me, despite what some coupon sites say). After you verify, you get a single-use 10% off promo code for one online order. It covers active-duty service members, retirees, reservists, veterans, and military spouses and registered dependents — and Timberland extends the same 10% to first responders, healthcare workers, teachers, and students. You can re-verify for a fresh code once every 30 days.

Here’s the honest catch: the discount is modest (10%), it’s online only, and it can’t be combined with any sale or other promotion. Because Timberland’s iconic 6-inch boots are sold everywhere, a retailer sale often beats the 10% code — Foot Locker, Champs, and others routinely mark 6-inch boot colorways down to $110–$170, past 10% off a $198 boot.

There are also deeper gated routes: the GovX military/government marketplace and, for eligible pros, ExpertVoice (up to 60% off). This is an independent guide — we’re not affiliated with Timberland, VF Corporation, SheerID, GovX, or ExpertVoice, and terms can change at any time.
aaa-military-discount: AAA offers a military membership discount for active-duty service members, retirees, and veterans — but because AAA is a federation of independently run regional clubs, the exact discount, how you enroll, and how your status is verified depend on which AAA club covers your area. Several clubs offer a discount on first-year membership dues, often bundled with perks like a free upgrade to AAA Plus, 20% off AAA-branded merchandise, and a recurring membership discount for your household.

You can typically enroll online at aaa.com/military (where eligibility is verified through ID.me), through GovX.com (verified by GovX ID, in most states), or by visiting an AAA branch or calling 800-922-8228 — and some clubs only offer the military rate in-branch or by phone, not online. Eligibility generally covers active duty (including Reserves and National Guard), retirees, and honorably discharged veterans.
This is an independent guide, not affiliated with AAA. Always confirm the current offer with your local AAA club before joining — terms differ by region and AAA can change them at any time.
acme-tools-military-discount: Does Acme Tools offer a military discount? No. Acme Tools does not run a first-party military or veteran discount — there is no service-verified program through ID.me, GovX, or SheerID, no military-discount page on acmetools.com, and Acme is not a seller on the GovX military marketplace. ID.me itself confirms it is "not aware that Acme Tools offers Military discounts." If a coupon site shows you an "Acme Tools military promo code," it is not a real military offer — those are generic codes that expire.

That does not mean you pay full price. Because Acme’s checkout is separate from cashback portals, a service member’s best move is to route the purchase through the highest-paying cashback site for that brand (Rakuten pays up to 2.5% on DEWALT, Milwaukee, Metabo HPT, and Stihl), stack it on any Acme sale price and coupon, and use Acme’s 30-day price-match guarantee if you find the identical model cheaper at another authorized dealer.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Acme Tools, and Acme controls its pricing and can change any term at any time.
sea-life-aquarium-military-discount: SEA LIFE aquariums offer a military discount you buy online through ID.me — not at the ticket window. It is open to a wide group: active duty, retirees, veterans, military spouses, and dependents, and it usually covers up to 4 people per order (kids age 1 and under are free and do not count).

ID.me lists the saving as "up to 25%," but the exact price is set by each aquarium and shown after you verify. A few locations (like Mall of America) also offer an in-person military rate ($18.99 + tax).
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with SEA LIFE or Merlin Entertainments, which controls the terms and can change them at any time; pricing varies by location.
husky-liners-military-discount: Here’s the honest answer: Husky Liners does not offer a military or veteran discount. There’s no military verification at checkout, no military page on huskyliners.com, and no partnership with ID.me, GovX, SheerID, or WeSalute — Husky Liners has no store on any of those platforms. So there’s nothing to verify and no military code to enter. Anyone advertising a “10%–25% military discount” or “15% off via ID.me” is repeating a coupon-site fabrication — one of those very pages even admits in the same breath that “there is no official Husky Liners military program.”

That doesn’t mean you overpay. Husky Liners is a RealTruck brand, and like RealTruck’s other lines its products are price-protected (MAP) — so the same WeatherBeater liners cost about the same everywhere, and shipping is free on every order. On a full-price item, the most reliable save is a cashback portal (TopCashback was 4% as of July 15, 2026), and the deepest cuts come from Husky Liners’ own public sales (front+rear combo and holiday markdowns), which everyone gets. If you specifically want an actual military discount on floor liners or mats, you’ll find it at a substitute brand with a GovX program — 3Wliners and SmartLiner both verify military status through GovX ID on their own products.
This is an independent guide — we’re not affiliated with Husky Liners or RealTruck — and terms can change at any time.
seatgeek-military-discount: SeatGeek offers a military discount for eligible active-duty service members and U.S. military veterans — but it works differently from most. There is no public promo code and no ID.me or GovX login. Instead, you request it directly through SeatGeek’s support chat, and SeatGeek may ask you to verify your military status before applying it. SeatGeek states the discount is typically for your first SeatGeek purchase, is one-time use, and may apply only to eligible events and ticket listings.

Importantly, SeatGeek does not publish the discount amount. Coupon sites that advertise a specific figure such as "5% off, up to $20" or "up to 20% off via ID.me" are not citing SeatGeek — and ID.me’s own SeatGeek page says it is not aware of any SeatGeek military discount. Treat those numbers as unconfirmed, and ask SeatGeek’s chat what your actual offer is.

This is an independent guide. We are not affiliated with SeatGeek. SeatGeek sets and can change these terms at any time; the amount is not publicly published and is determined in the support chat — confirm current details before you buy.
le-creuset-military-discount: Le Creuset does not offer an official military or veteran discount. There is no military verification page on lecreuset.com, and ID.me — the service most brands use for this — explicitly says it is not aware of a Le Creuset military offer. The "10% off with ID.me" you’ll see on coupon sites is not real; don’t count on it at checkout.

What does save real money: Le Creuset’s Factory to Table Sale and outlet stores routinely take 30–40%+ off with no ID required — deeper than any nominal military discount — and if you’re exchange-eligible, the Navy Exchange and AAFES stock Le Creuset sales-tax-free. Some Le Creuset outlet stores also honor an in-store 15% military offer on full-price items (varies by location).
NavyWeek is an independent guide and is not affiliated with Le Creuset. Le Creuset controls its pricing and can change it at any time.
phoenix-zoo-military-discount: Yes — the Phoenix Zoo gives military members and veterans (18+) $5 off general admission at the gate with valid photo ID, and runs free admission on Veterans Day and Memorial Day with military ID or DD214.

The everyday $5 is gate-only and can’t be used on online or advance tickets, so on regular days it’s worth comparing against the online advance price — the two don’t stack. The bigger wins are the free holiday days, and on Memorial Day the cardholder’s party also gets $10 off for up to four guests.

This is an independent guide; we’re not affiliated with the Phoenix Zoo, which is a nonprofit that sets and can change these terms each year. Confirm the current-year holiday terms on the zoo’s event pages before you go.
american-girl-military-discount: American Girl offers an official 15% military discount — published on its own FAQ and valid through December 31, 2026. Show a military ID in store, or enter a promotion code online at americangirl.com. Per American Girl’s wording it’s for active or retired members of the US Armed Forces; it excludes several collections and services and can’t be combined with other offers.
There’s also a tax-free route: the Navy Exchange and select AAFES/MCX locations carry American Girl. For excluded items — or just to skip sales tax — the Exchange can beat the 15%.
This is an independent guide from NavyWeek. We are not affiliated with American Girl or Mattel, which sets and can change these terms at any time (the offer ends 12/31/2026).
saatva-military-discount: Yes — the Saatva military discount is real and published: verified military members get a flat $225 off any order of $1,000 or more, year-round, through ID.me at checkout on saatva.com. Active duty, reservists, National Guard, veterans, and retirees all qualify — but Saatva is explicit that the military tier does not extend to spouses or dependents.

Here’s the part that saves you real money: the military discount can’t be combined with any other promotion, and Saatva almost always has a sitewide sale running. As of July 14, 2026, its 16th Anniversary Sale takes 15% off orders over $1,000 (through July 16, 2026) — on a $2,000 mattress that’s $300 off, which beats the $225 military discount. The honest rule: if your cart tops about $1,500 during a 15% sale, take the sale and skip the military discount; below $1,500, or between sales, the $225 is your floor.

This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Saatva or ID.me; Saatva controls these offers and can change them at any time, so always confirm current terms on Saatva’s official pages before you buy.
vortex-optics-military-veteran: Vortex Optics thanks current and retired U.S. military and law enforcement with a verification-gated discount program on Vortex products. Rather than a single public coupon, Vortex routes eligible shoppers to four verified programs — ExpertVoice, GovX, Scheels (via ID.me), and AAFES — where, after you confirm your service status, member pricing unlocks. The most widely published figure is 40% off MSRP, stated for the Scheels channel of the Vortex Discount Program.

To use it, you register and verify your status with one of the programs, then shop Vortex through that program’s site. There’s no walk-in code; the discount is tied to your verified account. First responders — firefighters, police officers, EMTs, and 911 dispatchers — are eligible through the Scheels channel.

This is an independent guide, not affiliated with Vortex Optics. Vortex and its partner programs control eligibility and terms and can change them at any time — always confirm details on the official program pages before purchasing.
seaworld-military-discount: SeaWorld’s Waves of Honor program is one of the strongest military offers in the theme-park world — and it’s real, run by SeaWorld’s parent United Parks & Resorts and verified through ID.me on SeaWorld’s own site. If you’re active-duty U.S. military, an activated or drilling reservist, or National Guard, you get one free single-day admission per year for yourself plus up to three direct dependents, so an entire family of four can visit free. You can also add up to six guest tickets at 50% off. The free active-duty offer is valid through December 31, 2026.

Veterans and retirees don’t get year-round free admission, but there are two strong routes: SeaWorld runs an annual free-admission window for veterans (plus up to three guests) during Military Appreciation Month in May, and year-round you can get 50% off single-day tickets (up to six) or a Military Silver Annual Pass for $161 (regularly $279) with unlimited visits, free parking, and in-park discounts.

You verify once through ID.me, then bring a valid U.S. military ID or proof of service to the gate. This is an independent guide — we’re not affiliated with SeaWorld, United Parks & Resorts, or ID.me, and terms can change at any time.
mattress-firm-military-discount: Yes — Mattress Firm offers a real military discount of 10-20% off top mattress and bedding brands, for active and reservist military, veterans, and military spouses (Mattress Firm’s page also says "and more"), verified through ID.me and usable online or in store. It’s published on Mattress Firm’s own site.

The catch is in the details: the 20% isn’t universal. Purple is reported to be capped at 10%, and several premium brands, plus clearance, floor models, and adjustable bases, are reported to be excluded. And because the discount applies to the listed sale price and generally won’t stack with other promotions, a deep seasonal sale — which Mattress Firm runs often — can sometimes match or beat the military 20%, so it’s worth comparing before you buy.

This is an independent guide, not affiliated with Mattress Firm. Mattress Firm controls the terms and can change them at any time — confirm the exact discount, brand tiers, and exclusions on its ID.me storefront before you buy.
marsupial-gear-military-discount: Straight answer: Marsupial Gear offers a military, veteran, and first-responder discount — but it's handled the old-fashioned way. There's no ID.me or GovX button. You create an account with the email you'll order under, then email proof of your ID or employment to sales@marsupialgear.com, and Marsupial applies a discount to your account.

The one catch: Marsupial doesn't publish the discount percentage. You'll learn the exact figure when their team replies. Eligible groups are U.S. first responders, U.S. active-duty military, and veterans. Because the amount is discretionary, it's worth comparing it against any live public promo code or sale before you buy.

This is an independent guide — NavyWeek is not affiliated with Marsupial Gear, and the brand can change or discontinue its discount at any time. Confirm current terms at marsupialgear.com before relying on them.
bath-and-body-works-military-discount: Bath & Body Works does not offer a military discount — no in-store ID discount, no SheerID or ID.me checkout, nothing on Veterans Day from the brand itself. ID.me’s own page for the brand says it isn’t aware of any military offer, and the "10% with military ID" claims on coupon sites have no source. We checked.

Here’s what the military community actually gets: 5% off Bath & Body Works gift cards through GovX (works online and in-store, on top of any sale), tax-free Bath & Body Works shopping at the military exchanges — the Navy Exchange carries 400+ B&BW items online and AAFES has opened B&BW stores on bases — and the brand’s own aggressive public promos (Buy 3 Get 1 Free, the twice-a-year Semi-Annual Sale at up to 75% off) that stack with cashback and the free rewards program.
This is an independent guide; we’re not affiliated with Bath & Body Works, GovX, or the Exchange. Terms change — confirm before you buy.
ford-military-discount: Ford Motor Company thanks those who serve through its Military Recognition Program, which provides an Exclusive Cash Reward toward the purchase or lease of an eligible new Ford or Lincoln vehicle. The reward is set by region and program period, so Ford does not publish one national figure — you see your offer after verifying your military status and entering your ZIP code at Ford’s official program site.

Eligibility is broad: active-duty service members, retirees, recently separated veterans, and their spouses, surviving spouses, and household members can all qualify. You confirm your status online through Ford’s verification partner, ID.me, then bring your emailed Certificate to a Ford or Lincoln dealer to apply the reward to your deal.

This is an independent guide to Ford’s program, not affiliated with Ford Motor Company. Ford sets and controls all program terms, amounts, and eligible vehicles, and can change them at any time — always confirm your exact offer at fordrecognizesu.com/military and with your dealer before you buy.
fjallraven-military-discount: Straight answer: Fjällräven does not run a standard military discount. There’s no ID.me, GovX, or SheerID checkbox on fjallraven.com, and no military promo code.

What Fjällräven has instead is the Industry Pro Program — and this is the key detail most sites miss. Its eligible categories do include military (active duty, reserves, veterans) and first responders (police, fire, EMS, paramedics) — but it’s an application-based pro program for full-time professionals. You must submit proof of full-time employment (a paystub), wait 4–6 weeks, and approval isn’t guaranteed. Fjällräven doesn’t publish the discount percentage.

For most people, the better move is Fjällräven’s seasonal sale and outlet (reported up to ~50% off) or buying the same gear at a retailer that offers an instant military discount (like Moosejaw or Backcountry via ID.me). This is an independent guide — NavyWeek is not affiliated with Fjällräven, and Fjällräven can change its programs at any time.
mcafee-military-discount: Yes, McAfee offers a military discount — but with a big caveat every coupon site skips: it runs entirely through ID.me, applies to 10-Device McAfee Total Protection, and McAfee never shows the price or percentage until after you verify. So ignore any page quoting a fixed "20% off" or "50% off" McAfee military discount — none of those numbers are confirmed by McAfee or ID.me, and they contradict each other.

Here’s the honest money move: McAfee already discounts the first year roughly 50-64% for everyone — the deals page anchor was $39.99 for the first term (renewing at $109.99/yr) on July 18, 2026 — and pays generous cashback through portals like Rakuten and Swagbucks (up to ~40% seen). For most people, the public first-year price bought through a cashback portal beats an unverifiable military-only rate, and it’s the path least likely to have cashback voided, since identity-gated checkouts typically break portal tracking.

If you have (or want) an ID.me account, by all means verify and look: then compare the revealed price head-to-head against the public deal before you pay. And whichever path you take, re-shop every renewal — the ~$109.99 auto-renew rate is almost never the best available price.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek.org is not affiliated with McAfee; McAfee sets and can change all terms at any time.
breville-military-discount: Breville does not offer a military or veteran discount. There’s no military checkout on breville.com, no Breville storefront on GovX, and ID.me itself confirms it isn’t aware of any Breville military offer. So the honest question isn’t "what’s the code?" — it’s "what’s the cheapest legitimate way for a service member to buy a Breville?"

The answer is usually Breville’s own Certified Remanufactured store, where a rebuilt Barista Express recently sold for about $469 vs $699.95 new, backed by a 6-month Breville warranty. If you want brand-new, public seasonal sales and Amazon (around $499–$549) beat anything a military shopper could unlock. The Navy Exchange and AAFES carry Breville tax-free, but their sticker can run higher than breville.com — so that path only wins with an exchange price-match.

This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Breville, and Breville controls and can change its terms at any time. Any site prompting you to "verify military status for a Breville discount," or advertising a "BETTERBREW military" or "Breville GovX" deal, is not describing a real Breville program.
american-trucks-military-discount: AmericanTrucks has an official Military & First Responder Cash Rewards Program — but it’s store credit, not an instant discount. Once you verify through SheerID, you earn 5% AT Cash sitewide, 10% on select Turn5-owned brands, or 20% on Open Box, calculated on your order’s post-coupon price.

The catch: rewards post after your order ships and must be spent on a future order within 90 days. That makes the program excellent for anyone building a truck or Jeep over time, and less useful for a one-and-done buy. Best of all, AT Cash stacks on top of AmericanTrucks’ frequent public promo codes.

This is an independent guide. We’re not affiliated with AmericanTrucks or Turn5, and AmericanTrucks controls the reward tiers, provider, and expiry and can change them at any time. Always confirm current terms on the program page before you buy.
omaha-steaks-military-discount: Omaha Steaks offers a real, official military discount: $10 off any order of $79 or more, verified through ID.me for active-duty, veterans, retirees, reservists, and military spouses and dependents. You verify once and can reuse it on omahasteaks.com, the app, or at participating retail locations.

The honest part most guides skip: Omaha Steaks is a perpetual-sale brand, and the $10 credit can’t be combined with its package sales or public promo codes. On most orders, the public sale price plus a public code saves more than $10 — so compare both totals and take the lower.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Omaha Steaks, and Omaha Steaks can change its terms at any time.
7-brew-military-discount: The honest answer: 7 Brew does not have an everyday military or veteran discount. What it does have is a Veterans Day (November 11) promotion you claim in person at the drive-thru with a valid military or veteran ID — and the deal changes each year (it was 50% off any drink in 2025 and 25% off in 2024).

For every other day of the year, your best savings at 7 Brew come from the free 7 Brew Rewards program in the 7 Brew app, not from a military discount. There is no military promo code and no online military-verification partner — no ID.me, GovX, SheerID, or WeSalute.
This is an independent guide from NavyWeek. We are not affiliated with 7 Brew Coffee, and 7 Brew sets and can change all terms at any time — Veterans Day terms change yearly and can vary by location.
tumi-military-discount: Does TUMI offer a military discount? No. TUMI has no military or veteran discount on tumi.com — there’s no verification gate (ID.me, SheerID, or otherwise) anywhere in checkout — and ID.me, the verification service coupon sites keep pointing to, states plainly that it isn’t aware of any TUMI military offer. Ignore the "20% military promo code" and "40% military discount" listings on coupon aggregators; they’re invented.

What military shoppers do have: a TUMI storefront on GovX with member pricing (the exact discount isn’t published), tax-free TUMI luggage at the military exchange — AAFES stocks the Alpha and Voyageur lines online — and, the biggest lever of all, TUMI’s public Semi-Annual Sale, up to 40% off select styles every January and July, which beats anything gated behind a military ID.
This is an independent guide; NavyWeek is not affiliated with TUMI, GovX, or AAFES, and each controls its own terms and can change them at any time.
rosetta-stone-military-discount: Straight answer: Rosetta Stone advertises a small 10% military discount (for Active Duty and Military Retirees, verified — WeSalute is its official verification partner), and WeSalute lists a Lifetime "Unlimited Languages" plan for $149 (no renewal fee). But here’s what coupon pages skip: Rosetta Stone runs near-constant public sales that drop that same Lifetime plan to roughly $149–$199 for everyone, so the military price is about what the general public already pays — and the 10% code off list is marginal and may not even stack on sale or lifetime pricing.

The old "Rosetta Stone is free for the military" line is mostly outdated. The DoD-wide free program lapsed years ago; today the standard free language benefit through MWR digital libraries is usually Transparent Language Online, not Rosetta Stone. Some base libraries and education centers still carry Rosetta Stone — so check locally before you buy.
This is an independent guide (not affiliated with Rosetta Stone, which is owned by IXL Learning); verify current prices at rosettastone.com before purchasing.
blade-hq-military-discount: Blade HQ does offer a Military and Law-Enforcement discount — but it is not a flat percentage and there is no automatic code. You email questions@bladehq.com or call 1-888-252-3347, verify your status, and Blade HQ quotes a discount on an item-by-item basis. The catch: the discount varies by product and excludes many items entirely, especially the premium name-brand knives whose prices are locked by the manufacturer (MAP). On those, the discount is frequently $0.

That means the honest best move for most shoppers is not the military discount at all — it is the free Blade Club loyalty program, which gives you roughly 2.5%–3.5% back in points, free domestic shipping, and a 1,000-point signup bonus, works automatically, and applies even to full-price MAP knives. Use the military quote only when you are buying a non-MAP or Blade HQ Exclusive item, then compare it to the current sale price.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Blade HQ; Blade HQ sets and can change these terms at any time.
liberty-university-military-discount: Liberty University’s military "discount" is a reduced military tuition rate for its online (LUO) programs — and it’s a big one. For 2026-27, eligible military students pay $250 per credit hour for undergraduate, $310 for master’s, and $395 for doctoral courses, versus standard online rates of roughly $390-455, $580-645, and $610-675 respectively. That works out to about 36% off undergraduate, 47% off master’s, and 35% off doctoral tuition.

The undergraduate $250 rate is deliberately set to match the federal Tuition Assistance (TA) cap, so active-duty students using TA can often cover undergraduate tuition with little or nothing out of pocket. The rate is open to active duty, Reserve/National Guard, veterans and retirees, their spouses, and current DoD government employees — and military children get 15% off standard tuition.

This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Liberty University, and Liberty sets and changes these rates annually — confirm current-year rates and your eligibility with Liberty’s Office of Military Affairs.
hooters-military-discount: Hooters’ headline military offer is its Veterans Day free meal: every November 11, veterans and active-duty and retired service members can pick one free entrée from a special menu when they dine in and buy a beverage, with a valid military ID or proof of service. That’s the offer Hooters actually publishes.

Beyond Veterans Day, you’ll see claims of a "10% daily / 20% off Tuesday" military discount. Hooters corporate does not publish an everyday military discount — where it exists, it’s offered at the discretion of individual (often franchised) locations. So call or ask your local Hooters before you count on it.

This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Hooters, and Hooters controls its offers and can change them at any time. Confirm the current terms on Hooters’ Military and Veterans page before you go.
ray-ban-military-discount: Ray-Ban partners with ID.me to offer savings to the military community. According to ID.me, verified military members — along with nurses, first responders, teachers, medical providers, and government employees — can unlock a Ray-Ban discount by verifying their status through ID.me at checkout on ray-ban.com. The catch worth knowing up front: Ray-Ban does not publish the exact discount percentage on its own website or on ID.me’s rendered offer page, so the rate you see should be confirmed at checkout. Many coupon sites quote "15%" (and some "up to 30%"), but those figures are not confirmed by Ray-Ban or by ID.me’s official terms.

Two things are clearly documented and important: Ray-Ban Meta AI smart glasses do not carry a military discount — ID.me states it is not aware of one, and Ray-Ban’s terms exclude Meta from promotions — and Ray-Ban discounts cannot be combined with other coupons or sale offers. Whether military spouses or dependents qualify is not stated by any source, so check directly through ID.me rather than assuming.

This is an independent guide to help you use the offer. We’re not affiliated with Ray-Ban, and Ray-Ban controls the terms and can change them at any time. Always confirm the live discount at ray-ban.com checkout via ID.me before you buy.
fanatics-military-discount: Fanatics gives verified members of the military and first responder communities 15% off all orders at Fanatics.com, on top of free U.S. shipping. The discount covers most officially licensed sports gear on the site — NFL, MLB, NBA, NHL, college, soccer, and more — with gift cards the main exclusion.

To use it, you shop normally and then verify your status with ID.me at checkout. Active duty, National Guard, veterans, retirees, and military spouses and dependents qualify under Troop ID; police, firefighters, EMTs, paramedics, and other first responders (active or retired), along with their spouses and immediate families, qualify under First Responder ID.

This is an independent guide compiled by NavyWeek. We’re not affiliated with Fanatics; Fanatics sets the terms and can change them at any time. Always confirm details on Fanatics’ official discount page before you buy.
titan-fitness-military-discount: Does Titan Fitness offer a military discount? No. As of July 14, 2026, Titan Fitness does not offer a military, veteran, or first-responder discount — and that is not a coupon-site coverage gap, it is the company’s own published policy. Titan’s support article "Military, Veteran, and First Responder Discount Policy" states it does not currently have a discount program for these groups, though it says it hopes to have a dedicated program in place in the near future.

If you have seen "Get 65% Off with Titan Fitness Military Discount" or "military codes" like AMRAP and SHOP20 on coupon sites, treat them as noise: Titan has no military program to attach a code to, so any "Titan Fitness military discount code" is a mislabeled public coupon at best and a fabrication at worst. Also, do not confuse Titan Fitness with "Titan BattleGear" or "Titan Wellness" on GovX — those are unrelated companies.

The good news: Titan is a value-priced brand that discounts hard in public. The real savings play is timing a sale event (Memorial Day, July 4, and Black Friday/Cyber Monday are its big windows), using the email-signup welcome code on a first order, and invoking the price-adjustment policy if the price drops right after you buy. crocs-military-discount: Crocs gives verified military members and veterans 15% off as their everyday rate. The good news: service members can still save real money at Williams Sonoma. This independent guide shows the honest best paths — the free Key Rewards program, the deep Outlet / Open Box clearance, a public welcome code, and the Professional Chefs trade program (for culinary pros, not military) — with links to Williams Sonoma’s official pages so you can confirm current terms before you buy.
nectar-military-discount: Does Nectar offer a military discount? Yes — but not the "40% off" you see in the banner. That 40–50% is Nectar’s public, everyone-gets-it sale. The actual military benefit is an extra 5% off Nectar’s best current sale price, unlocked by verifying your status on nectarsleep.com.

The good news for mattress shoppers: that 5% is written as "extra 5% off our best onsite offer," so it stacks on top of the current sale — which is unusual, since most mattress brands’ military discounts exclude sale items. It will not combine with other promo codes, and it is online-only.

This is an independent guide, not affiliated with Nectar. Because Nectar is on sale almost year-round, the honest best path is simple: buy during a deep sale and add your verified 5% on top. We link to Nectar’s official pages so you can confirm current terms before you buy.
bank-of-america-military-discount: Bank of America has no military discount — no code, no percent-off. What it has is a split personality. Its SCRA program is real and published: a 6% interest cap on accounts you opened before active duty (4% on a mortgage BofA owns and services), waived checking and ATM fees, and benefits that generally run six months past your active-duty end date on credit cards.

Its Military Lending Act fee handling is another story — the least consistent of any major issuer. BofA publishes no fee-waiver policy at all. Cardholder reports point to an unofficial pattern: annual fees over $100 (like the $550 Premium Rewards Elite) usually get charged and then auto-credited as “MLA CREDIT – ANNUAL FEE,” while the $95 Premium Rewards and $95 Alaska Airlines cards are simply charged. At least one servicemember got only $450 of $550 back. If a guaranteed $0-fee premium card is what you want, Amex publishes that deal and Chase’s is letter-confirmed — Bank of America doesn’t promise it, so open a BofA card only if you’re prepared to pay the fee.

This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Bank of America; BofA sets its practices — including the unpublished MLA fee-credit behavior — and can change them without notice, and the underlying rights come from federal law (SCRA and MLA) and your service dates.
reef-military-discount: Does REEF offer a military discount? Not on reef.com. There’s no military verification at REEF’s checkout, and ID.me Shop — the biggest military discount marketplace — says it’s not aware of any REEF military offer (checked July 14, 2026). The 20% code you may have seen advertised is REEF’s student and teacher discount through Student Beans, not a military program.

Military shoppers still have two real routes: the REEF storefront on GovX, where verified military, veterans, first responders, law enforcement, and government employees get member pricing on current styles, and REEF’s deep public sale section, which — combined with a cashback-portal click-through — usually beats everything else. There’s also a REEF offer inside WeSalute’s paid BenefitHub marketplace, but the amount isn’t published and membership starts at $9.99/month, so it only makes sense if you already subscribe.

This is an independent guide; NavyWeek is not affiliated with REEF, GovX, WeSalute, or Student Beans, and every program here can change its terms at any time. Use the decision table and chooser below to find your cheapest path on the exact pair you want.
audi-military-discount: Yes — Audi offers a genuine, brand-published military benefit called the Audi Military Select Program: a $1,000 bonus toward the lease or purchase of a select new, unused 2025 or 2026 Audi. It’s open to active-duty service members, veterans, retirees, National Guard and Reserve, military spouses and immediate family, and surviving spouses, and you claim it by verifying with ID.me to get a 6-character code you take to a participating Audi dealer. The current offer runs January 6, 2026 – January 4, 2027.

Here’s the honest part most coupon pages skip: the $1,000 is bonus cash, not a percentage off, and it is almost never the biggest lever on an Audi deal. The real move for a stateside buyer is to stack that $1,000 on top of whatever public lease, APR, or customer-cash incentive Audi is running that month — those are frequently worth more. And if you’re stationed or deployed overseas, the tax-free factory-direct Military AutoSource program can beat a stateside deal by far more than $1,000.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Audi; Audi controls the program and can change its terms at any time.
figs-military-discount: FIGS gives a 15% discount on most products to U.S. service members. The offer covers active-duty, veteran, and retired individuals with a U.S. military service record active from 9/30/1985, as well as USAA members. You confirm your status through ID.me during online checkout, and the discount applies automatically to eligible items.

The discount works only on the FIGS online store — it is not available in the FIGS mobile app, and it is U.S. only. It cannot be combined with other codes or applied to items already on sale, so during a site-wide promotion you’ll choose between the sale price and the military discount.
This is an independent guide, not affiliated with FIGS. FIGS sets the terms and can change them at any time; we cite FIGS’s own pages and its verification partner, ID.me.
rudis-military-discount: Yes — RUDIS offers a 10% military discount and a matching 10% first-responder discount. You verify your status through SheerID (RUDIS does not use GovX or ID.me), and after a quick document check you get a single-use code to enter at checkout on RUDIS.com. The military program covers active-duty service members, veterans, reservists, National Guard, and military dependents; the first-responder program covers firefighters, EMS/EMTs, and law enforcement.

Ten percent is the real number — ignore coupon sites advertising “25% or 50% off military,” which are just confusing RUDIS’s public Outlet markdowns with the military benefit. In fact, for prior-season gear the RUDIS Outlet (up to 50% off) often saves more than the 10% code, though outlet sales are final. Our rule: if the exact item you want is in the Outlet, buy it there; otherwise verify with SheerID for 10% off a current-season, returnable purchase.
NavyWeek is an independent guide and is not affiliated with RUDIS; RUDIS sets the terms and can change them at any time.
aarp-military-discount: Searching "AARP military discount"? Here’s the honest answer: AARP is not a store, so there’s no military discount code for merchandise. AARP is a nonprofit membership organization for adults 50 and older. What actually exists is a discounted membership rate for the military community — 5 years for $55 ($11/yr), 3 years for $38, or 1 year for $15 — plus a set of free veteran resources (job help, caregiving support, VA-benefits guidance, fraud protection) and a curated directory of military discounts at other brands.

One key thing most pages get wrong: you don’t have to be military — or even 50 — to join AARP. Anyone 18+ can join at $16/yr, and the standard $15 first-year rate is the same price the military 1-year offer gives you. Where the military offer genuinely wins is on the multi-year rate ($11/yr over five years).
This is an independent guide, not affiliated with AARP. AARP sets and can change these terms at any time; confirm current pricing at aarp.org before joining.
napa-military-discount: NAPA Auto Parts offers a military discount of about 10% in store at participating locations — bring a valid military ID and ask at checkout. Because NAPA stores are independently owned and operated, most (but not all) honor it, and it’s an in-person benefit: it generally isn’t available on napaonline.com. There’s no ID.me, GovX, or SheerID military verification for NAPA — ID.me’s own site says it isn’t aware NAPA offers a military discount.

Here’s the honest part: for most shoppers the military discount isn’t the best deal. NAPA regularly runs public codes for 20% off orders of $125 or more (plus a 20%-off-first-order email signup) on napaonline.com — open to everyone, no verification — and you can stack a cashback portal (Rakuten, BeFrugal) underneath. On a $200 parts order that’s roughly $40–$50 off versus $20 from the 10% military discount. So use the 10% when you’re buying in person (or buying items the online codes exclude); otherwise the public code wins.
This is an independent guide — we’re not affiliated with NAPA, ID.me, or any coupon site, and NAPA (and each independent store) controls the terms and can change them at any time.
toyota-military-discount: Toyota gives eligible service members and veterans a $500 Military Rebate toward a new Toyota when they buy or lease through Toyota’s financing. It is not a coupon or a percentage off the sticker — it is a $500 rebate applied at the dealership to your down payment (if you finance) or to the amount due at signing (if you lease), and it requires credit approval through Toyota Financial Services. Active-duty members, inactive reservists, retirees, veterans within two years of discharge, and their household and Gold Star family members can qualify.

How you prove eligibility depends on where you live. Most of the country uses Toyota’s ID.me verification, but five Southeast states (Alabama, Florida, Georgia, North Carolina, South Carolina) are served by a separate Southeast Toyota Finance $500 Military Rebate where you show proof of service directly to the dealer.

This is an independent guide from NavyWeek to help you understand the offer. We are not affiliated with Toyota, and Toyota controls the program and can change its terms at any time — always confirm current details with your local Toyota dealer before you sign.
fedex-military-discount: FedEx does not offer a military or veteran discount on shipping — there’s no military-ID, ID.me, or GovX program at FedEx Express, FedEx Ground, or FedEx Office. The real way service members and veterans save is the free FedEx Advantage program, which military-affiliated memberships like USAA unlock at enhanced rates (reported up to ~40% off Express and ~15% off Ground for personal shipping).

So the “military” angle is real but indirect: the discount comes from your USAA or association membership, not from FedEx honoring a military ID. And the exact percentage depends on the partner you enroll through and your shipment profile — FedEx publishes no single military number.
This is an independent guide from NavyWeek. We are not affiliated with FedEx, and FedEx (and USAA) control the terms and can change them at any time.
holiday-inn-express-military-discount: Holiday Inn Express — a select-service brand of IHG — offers a real Military Appreciation Rate you book on ihg.com. IHG publishes a floor of “minimum 5% off the Best Flexible Rate,” and the actual discount varies by hotel, date, and availability. It’s for leisure travel, open to US and Canadian active-duty, veteran, and retired service members plus their family members with valid ID, and you show a military or veteran ID at check-in. There’s also a separate Government Rate for travelers on official government or military orders, priced as a percentage off the Best Flex Rate that aligns toward the federal per-diem cap.

Here’s the honest part: hotel rates don’t stack, and the military rate cannot be combined with any other offer. Because it’s only a 5% floor, it’s frequently not the cheapest option — the Advance Purchase (Book Early & Save, roughly 10–15%) or a member sale rate often wins. So pull up the military rate and the other rates for your hotel and date, and book whichever is lowest. The real long-term win is a free IHG One Rewards account: book direct and every stay — including on the military rate — earns points (about 10 per dollar at Holiday Inn Express) and qualifying nights toward status, which compounds across all your trips.
This is an independent guide — we’re not affiliated with Holiday Inn Express, IHG, or IHG One Rewards, and IHG controls these rates and can change them at any time.
ghost-golf-military-discount: Yes — Ghost Golf offers a military discount verified through GovX, worth up to 20% off for active-duty service members, veterans, and first responders (immediate family included). Verify once at GovX, get a single-use code, and enter it at checkout on ghostgolf.com.

One tip: Ghost Golf also circulates public promo codes that sometimes run as deep as the military rate. Because a GovX code generally won’t stack with a public code, check both and use whichever saves more.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Ghost Golf; Ghost Golf sets and can change these terms at any time.
1st-phorm-military-discount: Does 1st Phorm offer a military discount? Straight answer: no. 1st Phorm has no military, veteran, or first-responder discount, and it goes further than most brands — it issues no coupons or discount codes of any kind. Its own discounts page says so directly: "We don’t give out coupons," because the company keeps one fair price all year instead of inflating prices and running "sales."

So if you see a "1st Phorm military discount code," a "first responder 70% off," or a "10% off coupon," know that 1st Phorm says those are not legitimate. There is no ID.me or GovX gate on the supplements. The real ways to save are open to everyone: order to $150 for free shipping (plus a free-gift tier), use autoship on staples, and lean on the 110% money-back guarantee if a product does not work for you.
This is an independent guide — NavyWeek is not affiliated with 1st Phorm, and the brand can change its policies at any time. Confirm current terms at 1stphorm.com.
atlantis-military-discount: Yes — Atlantis Paradise Island offers an official military discount: verify with ID.me and get up to 30% off Best Available Rates (the ID.me marketplace lists it as up to 25% for military; either way it’s "up to," not a flat rate). Teachers, nurses, and first responders get the same program. One disambiguation up front: this is the Bahamas resort — Atlantis The Palm and The Royal in Dubai are separate properties with separate offers.

But the biggest military-only play at Atlantis isn’t the discount at all. Caesars Rewards’ free Salute program gives US service members and veterans automatic Platinum status — and Caesars Platinum members can claim up to four complimentary nights a year at Atlantis’ Coral Towers, room and room taxes included, per Caesars help-center and editorial reporting. You’ll still pay the resort fee and gratuities, and the resort expects a few hours of casino play, but on a 4-night stay it beats the ID.me rate by roughly $1,400. Caesars’ own pages block automated checks, so confirm the current comp terms by phone before you plan around them.
This is an independent guide. We’re not affiliated with Atlantis, ID.me, or Caesars; the resort controls every offer and can change terms at any time.
cracker-barrel-military-discount: Cracker Barrel offers a 10% in-store discount to Cracker Barrel Rewards members who are active-duty, reserve, retired, or veteran members of the U.S. Armed Forces. You verify your service once through ID.me, link it to your Rewards account, and the discount applies automatically at the register on qualifying restaurant and retail purchases.

The discount is in-store only — it does not work on online orders, catering, delivery, or takeout — and excludes alcohol, gift cards, Meals for Two, Take Home Meals, taxes, delivery fees, and gratuities. You must be enrolled in Cracker Barrel Rewards and give your account to the cashier for the discount to apply.

This is an independent guide, not affiliated with Cracker Barrel. Cracker Barrel sets the terms and can change them at any time; verify details on Cracker Barrel’s official military discount page before you rely on them.
virgin-voyages-military-discount: Yes — Virgin Voyages has an official Military & First Responders Rate: 5%, 10%, or 15% off the retail voyage fare on select sailings, for US and Canadian active-duty members, veterans, military spouses, surviving spouses, and first responders. You apply it yourself with the Access Key SERVICERATE at checkout, and you verify the old-fashioned way — by showing your military or first-responder ID at the terminal when you check in. No ID.me, no SheerID.

Here’s the part most pages miss: Virgin is one of the few cruise lines whose military rate stacks with public sales. During promo windows like "70% Off 2nd Sailor," the terms on both offers explicitly allow combining — which turns a 15% thank-you into roughly 45% off the fare. The best strategy is almost never "military rate instead of the sale"; it’s the sale plus SERVICERATE.
NavyWeek is an independent guide, not affiliated with Virgin Voyages; Virgin controls these terms and can change them at any time.
vons-military-discount: Does Vons offer a military discount? Sort of — but not the flat percentage coupon sites promise. Vons, part of Albertsons Companies, runs a SheerID-verified community program that includes Military (along with first responders, teachers, students, seniors, and government-assistance recipients). Verifying unlocks exclusive member offers loaded to your Albertsons for U account — but neither Vons’ nor Albertsons’ official FAQ publishes a standing “10% off every order.”

The famous “Vons 10% military discount” actually traces to a temporary 2013 government-shutdown promotion, not a durable rule, so treat any flat number with caution. What reliably saves money is open to everyone: join the free Albertsons for U program, clip digital coupons, follow the weekly ad, and earn points toward grocery and gas rewards. If you have base access, compare the on-base commissary for staples.

This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Vons or Albertsons Companies, and they can change terms at any time. Member-offer values vary — confirm the live offer in your own for U account before you count on a number.
liberty-mutual-military-discount: Straight answer: Liberty Mutual does offer a Military Discount on auto insurance. Its discounts page salutes "those who are Active, Retired, or Reserved in the U.S. Armed Forces." But here is the honest part: Liberty Mutual does not publish a percentage. Auto-insurance discounts are rated by your state and personal profile, so any "12%" or "up to 25%" you see quoted online is not a number Liberty Mutual stands behind — the only real figure is the one on your personalized quote.

The military discount stacks with Liberty Mutual’s other discounts (multi-policy, multi-car, RightTrack telematics, claims-free, paperless), and that stack is what actually moves the price. For most of the military community, though, the bigger decision is which carrier — USAA typically prices lowest for eligible service members in 2026 comparisons, so quote Liberty Mutual’s military-discounted rate against USAA (and one or two others) before deciding.
This is an independent guide — we are not affiliated with Liberty Mutual. Confirm current terms at libertymutual.com.
montana-knife-company-military-discount: Montana Knife Company runs an official military and first-responder discount through GovX ID — verify once, get a code, and it applies to MKC products at checkout. Military.com lists the benefit as "up to 20%," but the exact live rate is only shown after you verify with GovX, so treat 20% as a ceiling rather than a guarantee.

Because MKC sells in fast, limited "drops" and does not stack codes, the practical play is to have your GovX discount ready before a drop goes live — if a model sells out, no discount can be applied retroactively.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Montana Knife Company, which controls the terms and can change them at any time; GovX sets the live discount rate.
our-place-military-discount: Our Place does offer a military discount: 10% off orders of $100 or more, verified through ID.me. It’s published on Our Place’s own site and covers military members, veterans, first responders, government employees, nurses, medical providers, teachers, and students.

Here’s the honest part most coupon pages skip: the ID.me 10% can’t be combined with any other offer, and Our Place runs frequent sitewide sales of 25–40% off. When a sale like that is live — which is often — the public sale is the better deal, because you can’t stack the 10% on top of it. So the smartest move is simple: take whichever single discount is deeper.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Our Place, and Our Place can change its terms at any time. Confirm the current offer on Our Place’s official ID.me page before you buy.
lenscrafters-military-discount: LensCrafters offers a real 15% military discount on eyewear (and 10% off contact lenses), verified free through ID.me at checkout. That’s the exact figure on LensCrafters’ own ID.me store page, and it’s open to the broader military community — but here’s the honest part most coupon sites skip: for LensCrafters it’s usually not your best price.

LensCrafters runs deep, almost-always-on public sales (currently around 40% off prescription glasses and 50% off lenses), and the 15% military discount can’t be combined with a sale or with vision insurance — so on a real cart, the public sale or your vision benefit almost always beats the 15%, and you have to choose one. If you carry TRICARE FEDVIP, EyeMed, or VSP, run the order through insurance. If you’re active duty, you can usually get prescription eyewear free through military optometry and shouldn’t pay retail at all. Use the 15% ID.me discount when you have no insurance and no live sale beats it.
This is an independent guide — we’re not affiliated with LensCrafters, ID.me, or TRICARE, and terms can change at any time.
royal-caribbean-military-discount: Royal Caribbean offers a reduced military rate — a lower cruise fare available on select sailings for active-duty service members, retirees, veterans with an Honorable Discharge, and the spouses of deployed or deceased military personnel. It works differently from a store coupon: the rate is applied to one stateroom, at least one eligible person must occupy that room, and you prove eligibility by showing your military ID or DD 214 at check-in — there’s no instant percentage-off code on Royal Caribbean’s own site.

Royal Caribbean does not publish a fixed percentage; military fares change by ship and date, so it pays to compare the military rate against the best current public promotion before you book. Crucially, if anyone in the room doesn’t meet the terms, Royal Caribbean can re-price the booking to the lowest available fare and bill you the difference — or deny boarding — so only book the military rate when you can document eligibility.

This is an independent guide to help you use the offer. We’re not affiliated with Royal Caribbean, and Royal Caribbean controls the terms and can change them at any time. Always confirm details on Royal Caribbean’s official special-pricing FAQ before you buy.
jetblue-military-discount: JetBlue offers one of the more generous standing military benefits among U.S. airlines, and it is confirmed on JetBlue’s own Military and Veteran Customers page: a 5% discount off base fares plus free checked bags. Active-duty service members traveling for leisure get 2 free checked bags (up to 50 lbs each); those traveling on orders or PCS get up to 5 free checked bags (up to 99 lbs each) — for themselves and dependents on the same itinerary.

The most important thing to know: you cannot book this discount online or at the airport. You have to contact JetBlue by phone or chat and have an agent apply it. Active-duty travelers verify with a DOD Common Access Card (plus travel orders for duty travel). Veterans and retirees get the same 5% + 2 free bags, but only through a paid WeSalute+ membership (formerly Veterans Advantage) — you provide your WeSalute+ Member ID when you book.

For most travelers the free checked bags are worth more than the 5% fare cut, especially on a PCS move. This is an independent guide — we’re not affiliated with JetBlue or WeSalute, and terms, fares, and bag fees can change at any time. Always confirm on JetBlue’s official site before you book.
grammarly-military-discount: Yes — Grammarly offers a real military discount: 50% off Grammarly Pro for your first subscription period, verified through SheerID. That takes the $144/year individual Pro plan down to about $72 for year one. After the first term it renews at the standard rate, and the discount covers only the first seat.

Ignore coupon sites quoting "40%" or "60%" — the verified figure from Grammarly’s own help center and SheerID is 50%. If you only need light grammar checking, Grammarly’s free plan may be all you need.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Grammarly; Grammarly sets and can change these terms at any time.
opticsplanet-military-discount: Yes — OpticsPlanet offers a service discount of up to 25% off select brands for active-duty military, veterans, first responders, and healthcare workers. The catch: it’s redeemed by phone, not online. You call OpticsPlanet’s hotline, give the representative the product code for what you want, and they apply the discount to your order. There’s no ID.me or GovX login on OpticsPlanet’s site for this — despite what some coupon pages claim.

Here’s the honest money-saving part: for the premium optics brands OpticsPlanet sells (Vortex, EOTech, Leupold, Sig, Aimpoint), the best deal is usually the brand’s own military/LE pro program, verified instantly online through GovX — it frequently matches or beats 25% and skips the phone call. If you’re not eligible for any service discount, stack an OpticsPlanet sale plus OpticsPlanet Bucks (2% back, more during Bonus Bucks events).
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with OpticsPlanet, and OpticsPlanet controls its terms and can change them at any time.
maurices-military-discount: Maurices does not run a published, company-wide military discount, and there’s no verified way to claim one online — ID.me itself says it isn’t aware of any Maurices military offer. What’s real is a 10% in-store discount at many participating Maurices stores: show a valid military ID at checkout and ask.

Because it’s store-by-store, it’s worth confirming with your local store before you count on it. Online, you’ll almost always save more by stacking a promo code on clearance than by chasing a “military” code that doesn’t exist there.
This is an independent guide from NavyWeek. We are not affiliated with Maurices, and Maurices (and each store) controls the terms and can change them at any time.
shark-ninja-military-discount: Does SharkNinja offer a military discount? Straight answer: not in the US. SharkNinja publishes no military or veteran discount on its US sites (sharkclean.com and ninjakitchen.com), and ID.me even says outright that it is "not aware that SharkNinja offers Military discounts." There is no US ID.me, GovX, or SheerID checkout discount for either the Shark or Ninja brand.

The "9% SharkNinja military discount" you will see in search is a UK-only program through GoCertify — its eligibility literally lists "R.A.F" and "Armed Forces Dependents" — and it does not apply to US shoppers. In the US, the real ways to save are public sales, certified-refurbished units, Amazon pricing with a cashback portal, and, if you already carry a paid WeSalute+ membership, occasional product-specific SharkNinja deals through its BenefitHub marketplace.

This independent guide explains the honest US-vs-UK split, who the WeSalute membership route actually covers, the aggregator claims to ignore, and the genuine ways for a service member to pay less on Shark and Ninja. NavyWeek is not affiliated with SharkNinja; terms change, so confirm current offers before buying.
stetson-military-discount: Does Stetson offer a military discount? No. As of July 14, 2026, Stetson does not offer a military, veteran, or first-responder discount — its FAQ and entire Help Center publish no such program, Stetson has no store on ID.me Shop, and there is no Stetson shop on GovX. The "10% via ID.me" you may have seen on coupon sites like SemperSave and WorthEPenny has no primary source behind it.

Here’s what actually works. Boot Barn, an authorized Stetson retailer, gives ID.me-verified military members and first responders 10% off all full-priced styles every day — online and in its stores — which makes it the real military route to a discounted Stetson hat. And Stetson’s own end-of-season sales run deep: a 40%-off EOS collection and an extra-25%-off-sale-items collection were live when we checked.
This is an independent guide; NavyWeek is not affiliated with Stetson or Boot Barn, and each company controls its terms and can change them at any time.
american-home-shield-military-discount: American Home Shield offers a genuine military discount: 20% off any home warranty plan for the first year if you’re a new member and an active-duty service member, veteran, reservist, or National Guard member (any branch). At renewal, that becomes $5 per month off for as long as you keep the plan. You verify with your military email at shopping.ahs.com/military — AHS does not use ID.me or GovX for this.

Here’s the honest part most pages skip: AHS also runs an always-on public "$150 off your first year" offer that anyone can use with no verification. On a mid-priced plan, that flat $150 slightly beats the 20% in year one. The military discount’s real advantage is the ongoing $5/month renewal credit — no public offer gives you anything after year one — plus it wins even in year one on a pricier ShieldPlatinum plan.
This is an independent guide. We’re not affiliated with American Home Shield, and AHS can change these terms at any time.
mavis-military-discount: Yes — Mavis Discount Tire gives 10% off to active duty military, reservists, and veterans, applied to your total before sales tax. The same 10% runs at Mavis’s sibling banners, NTB and Tire Kingdom. Show your military ID and tell the store manager at checkout — it is in-store only, not valid on online orders.

The catch worth knowing: the military discount cannot be combined with any Mavis coupon, promo code, or special offer, and Mavis runs frequent manufacturer tire rebates ($100–$160) and service coupons that are often bigger than 10%. So the smart move is not automatic — on a rebate-eligible tire or a coupon-eligible service, the deal frequently beats the flat military discount. We run the math below.
This is an independent guide. NavyWeek is not affiliated with Mavis, NTB, or Tire Kingdom; Mavis sets the terms and can change them at any time.
cub-cadet-military-discount: Cub Cadet does not give an instant military discount at checkout. Instead it runs an official Heroes Program rebate: $300 or $500 back (depending on model) for verified military and first responders who buy a qualifying PRO-series mower from a local Cub Cadet Independent Dealer.

The rebate is filed after you buy, within 30 days, at sbdheroprogram.com — and it only applies to premium PRO/PRO X and select zero-turn models, not homeowner riding or push mowers. If you’re buying qualifying equipment, it’s real money back; if you’re buying a homeowner model, the rebate won’t apply and seasonal offers are your best bet.

This is an independent guide. We’re not affiliated with Cub Cadet or Stanley Black & Decker, and the terms can change at any time. Always confirm current rebate amounts, dates, and qualifying models on sbdheroprogram.com before you buy.
reebok-military-discount: Reebok runs a Hero Discount program that gives military members, reservists, and veterans 30% off at reebok.com. Eligibility is confirmed through ID.me, the third-party identity service, during checkout — once verified, the discount applies automatically to your order.

The offer is for U.S. customers shopping online at www.reebok.com. It excludes clearance clothing styles and delivery charges, can’t be combined with other promotions, and isn’t valid on previous purchases. Reebok can change or end the program at any time, so confirm the current terms at checkout.
This is an independent guide from NavyWeek. We’re not affiliated with Reebok or ID.me; Reebok sets and controls all discount terms.

banana-republic-military-discount: Banana Republic offers a military discount for in-store purchases only — you show a valid military ID at the register, with no app, code, or online account.
